(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]Syrup of Lavender (Halhâl)[/b]\nTake a ratl of lavender and cook it in water to cover until its substance comes out. Then take the clear part of it and add it to a ratl of honey and cook all this until it takes the form of a syrup. Drink an ûqiya and a half of this with three of hot water. Its advantages are in cleaning the brain and the stomach; it lightens the body and dries up black bile gently, but it contracts the breath, and it is fitting to regulate the drink with the cheering drink or water of mufarrih (cheering).
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]Syrup of Lemon[/b]\nTake lemon, after peeling its outer skin, press it and take a ratl of juice, and add as much of sugar. Cook it until it takes the form of a syrup. Its advantages are for the heat of bile; it cuts the thirst and binds the bowels.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]A Syrup of Benefit Against the Burning of Jaundice and Ringworm[/b]\nTake juice pressed from shashtaraj (fumitory), which is known as "children's greens," and juice pressed from endive (chicory), which is known as taifaq, and juice pressed from borage, half a ratl of each. Boil it on the fire, clarify it and add a ratl of sugar. The bag: put in a ratl of the skin of yellow myrobalan, cooked until it falls apart and forced through a cloth. Cook all this until it takes the form of a syrup. Drink three ûqiyas of this in half a ratl of fresh milk.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]A Syrup which Dries Black Bile and Phlegm[/b]\nTake a ratl of basbâyij, peeled in its upper part, and another of sanâ, and half a ratl of agaric, and two ûqiyas each of fennel and ground licorice wood, and a handful each of lavender mashashtir, and spring cilantro. The bag: put an ûqiya of cinnamon and another of cloves, grind them coarsely and put them in the bag. Cook the roots in two ratls of water until their substance comes out, then take the clear part of it and add it to two ratls of honey and four more of sugar, and cook all this until it takes the form of a syrup. Drink three ûqiyas of this with half a ratl of hot water, after taking a few seeds of good musk. Its benefits: in all the heats of the body, in all black ringworm infections, and in phlegm; it cleans all the residues from the body and purges it gently for a good evacuation.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]Syrup of Jujubes[/b]\nTake two ratls of jujubes and an ûqiya each of purslane and lettuce; cook all this in five ratls of water, then clarify it and add it to two ratls of sugar, and cook until it takes the form of a syrup. Drink an ûqiya of it with three of cold water. It benefits in periodical fevers, purifies thick blood, calms the cough, cuts thirst, and lightens the constitution.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]Syrup of Thistle[/b]\nTake a ratl of thistle, ground coarsely, half a ratl of mashashtir, and an ûqiya of bay leaves, a handful which fills the hand of leaves from the interior of an orange tree, half an ûqiya each of anise, seeds of wild carrot, and seeds of dodder, an û qiya each of bitter and sweet almonds; pulverize all the roots and greens and cover them with three ratls of water in which black garbanzos have been steeped for a night and a day. Then put it in a new pot and cook until the water is reduced by half, then steep it and clarify it and take the clear part to add to a ratl of sugar and another of honey. The bag: half an ûqiya each of Indian spikenard, asârûn, and flower of cloves, and cook all this until it takes the form of a syrup. Drink an ûqiya and a half of it with three ûqiyas of hot water, and above all, if it is drunk in the bath, it has a greater effect, if it please God the Most High, praise be to Him.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]Syrup of Tamarind[/b]\nTake a ratl of tamarind and steep in five ratls of water, throw away the dregs immediately and add the clarified water to a ratl of sugar. Cook all this until it takes the form of a syrup. Drink two ûqiyas of it in three of cold water. It is beneficial in jaundice, and takes it away easily; it cuts bilious vomit and thirst, awakens the appetite to eat, and takes the bitterness of food out of the mouth.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]Syrup of Carrots[/b]\nTake four ratls of carrots, after removing the fibers that are in the centers, and cook them in water to cover until their substance comes out. Then take the clear part of it and add it to three ratls of honey, cleaned of its foam. The bag: ...[about three words missing]... an ûqiya of cubebs, two ûqiyas each of ginger and long pepper, and half an ûqiya of cinnamon and flower of cloves. Cook until it takes the form of a syrup. Drink an ûqiya of this with three of hot water: it is beneficial in the lack of urine, increases desire, and dissolves phlegm, heats the kidneys admirably, and likewise the other parts of the body, God willing.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]Syrup of Apples[/b]\nTake a ratl of sweet apples, those that the common people call sarîj, cook them in water to cover until they fall apart and their substance comes out, then clarify it and take the clear part and add it to a ratl of sugar. The bag: an ûqiya of aloe stems, pounded and put into the bag. Cook until it takes the form of a syrup. Drink an ûqiya in two of hot water. Its benefits: it fortifies and gladdens the heart.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]Carrot Paste[/b]\nTake a ratl of carrots, of which you have cleaned the interior. Cook it in a ratl of water, some two boilings, then take it off the fire and let it dry a little, over a sieve. Add it to three ratls of honey, cleaned of its foam, and cook all this until it takes the form of a paste. Then season it with ginger, galingale, cubeb and flowers, half an û qiya in all for each ratl. Eat it like a nut at meals. Its benefits: it fortifies coitus and increases desire beautifully; it is admirable.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]Green Walnut Paste[/b]\nTake a ratl of green walnuts and pierce them well with an iron skewer, then steep them in water for three days; take them out of the water and for each ratl take three of honey, cleaned of its foam, after cooking the nuts a little. Take them from the water and return them to the honey, and cook them until they take the form of a paste. Season with cinnamon, cloves, and ginger, three quarters of an ûqiya for each ratl, and eat it after meals. Its benefits: it excites the appetite and digests foods, heats the kidneys, and increases urine.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]Quince Paste[/b]\nTake a ratl of quince, cleaned of its seeds and cut into small pieces. Pound it well until it is like brains. Cook it with three ratls of honey, cleaned of its foam, until it takes the form of a paste. It is also made by another, more amazing recipe: take it as said before, and cook it in water alone until its essence comes out, clean the water of its sediments, and add it to as much sugar, and make it thin and transparent, without redness, and what you have made will remain in this state. Its benefits: it lightens the belly that suffers from bile, it suppresses bitterness in the mouth, and excites the appetite. And I say it keeps bad vapors from rising from the stomach to the brain.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]Paste of Honeyed Roses[/b]\nTake half a ratl of fresh roses and two ratls of honey; take the petals from the roses and scatter them in a ceramic cooking-pan; boil the honey on the fire and remove its foam; add the roses and boil it until it takes the aspect of a paste. Eat it like a nut at meals. Its benefits: for weak stomachs, for the liver, for the onset of dropsy of the lower belly, and it lightens the constitution moderately, God willing.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]Violet Paste[/b]\nTake a ratl of the flowers and three of honey, after removing its foam. Cook all this until it takes the form of a paste, and eat of it like a nut at meals. Its advantages: it counters dry coughs, softens the belly, cuts bilious thirst and cuts the bile that comes out, God willing.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]Mint Paste[/b]\nTake a ratl of green mint leaves and crush them gently; add three ratls of honey, cleaned of its foam, and blend it until it takes the form of a paste. Then season it with an û qiya of flower of cloves per ratl. Its benefits: it eases and aids against heaviness of the body and mind, aids in eardrum dropsy, dissolves phlegm in the various parts of the body, strengthens the urine, and cuts vomit; it is good with sweet grains of anise, eaten with them or after them. It is beneficial, God willing.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]Tîqantast Paste[/b]\nTake four ûqiyas of its outermost skin, after peeling it with iron knives, then pound it gently and cook it in water to cover; then add it to a ratl of honey, cleaned of its foam, and thicken it until it takes the form of a paste. Eat of it like a nut at meals. It benefits ...[one word missing]... dissolves phlegm in various parts of the body, awakens the appetite to eat, makes urine flow, aids in dropsy, and lightens the constitution mildly. In this it is admirable, God willing.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]A Paste which Fortifies the Stomach, the Liver, and the Brain[/b]\nTake habbat halâwa, caraway, fried cumin, and shuniz (nigella), four ûqiyas of each, pound all this and mix it with three ratls of honey, cleaned of its foam. Thicken it until it is a dough. Eat it like a nut at meals. Its benefits: in the winds of the body, it dissolves phlegm and digests foods, clears the head, lightens the body gently, aids in mild coughs, and dries black bile gently.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]Orange Paste[/b]\nTake the peel of red oranges, after steeping them in water, and cut them like fingers. Take a weight of one ratl and add to it three ratls of honey cleaned of its foam, until it takes the form of a paste. Eat of it like a nut at meals. Its benefits: it digests foods, dissolves phlegm, increases the urine, and aids in cold poisons; in this it is admirable.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]Electuary (Juwârish) of Mint[/b]\nTake a ratl of mint, pound it and press out its juice, add a ratl of sugar and a quarter of an ûqiya of mastic and make an electuary. Its benefits: it cuts phlegmatic vomiting, excites the appetite, heats the stomach, and if taken before eating, constipates the intestines; it is useful.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]Electuary of 'Ud Qimâri[/b]\nTake half an ûqiya of it, and of mastic, cinnamon, Chinese cinnamon, half an ûqiya each, two ratls of sugar and two more of rosewater. Put all this on the fire until it makes an electuary. Its benefits: it strengthens the heart and lightens the spirit, digests foods, lightens the body gently, strengthens the liver, dissolves phlegm in various parts of the body, and aids in dropsy.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]Electuary of Cloves[/b]\nTake two ûqiyas of its flowers and two ratls of sugar dissolved in rosewater; thicken it until it takes the form of a paste and make an electuary, in the form of fingers and tablets. Eat half an ûqiya of it at meals. Its benefits: it excites the appetite, dissolves phlegm, greatly gladdens, increases the force of coitus, and restrains the temperament.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]Electuary of Red Sandalwood[/b]\nTake three quarters of an ûqiya of red sandalwood, and a quarter of an ûqiya of tabashir (manna sugar). Pound all this and add it to a ratl and a quarter of sugar, dissolved in rosewater. Cook all this until it takes the form of juwarish and take it off the fire.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]Electuary of White Sandalwood[/b]\nTake an ûqiya of white sandalwood and a quarter of an ûqiya of tabashir, pound it all and sift it; add it to a ratl and a quarter of sugar and as much again of rosewater; cook it all until it makes juwarish.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]Another Delicate Medicinal Powder[/b]\nTake fennel, habbat halâwa and sugar, equal amounts, pound it all and mix it. Administer it in a powder at bedtime, in the amount of one handful. It cleans the head and the stomach and calms mild coughs, God willing.
(Andalusian, XIII c.)\n[b]Powders That Digest The Food[/b]\nTake four ûqiyas of mastic, pound it and add it as much sugar, and to both add an ûqiya of anise and another of fennel. Mix it all and administer half an ûqiya of it at bedtime.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]A Tarte of Fysch[/b]\nTak fygges & reysingis & cyng hem & do ther to freysch samoun or othyr maner of freysch fysch grynd alle to gyder temper hem up with almounde mylk & frye almounds in swete oyle & do therinne lye alle to gydr do ther to pouder of galingale reysings of coraunce quybybes & soden perys & schere hem & cast hem ther inne amonge alle to gidre & of ilk of the spyces kepe the halvendel with outen colour thi fars with saffroun & swet it with sugre. Tak laumpreys & laumprouws & elys & dares & roches & loches smeltys and other maner of freysch fysch & wete hem in flour frye hem in swete oyle & loke thu have dats farsed & plumbys damaycynis than go to the ovene & mak dowe & couche thi fars on this maner, fferst ley thi kake of dowe than tak thi fars & couche thi fryed fysch & thi dats farsed & plumbys & thi almondys & drengle it in swete oyle & poudre it with sugre & lay thou thi fars on this maner couche thi fars as thu wylt have hulke it & pinche it & mak thi lowes colour it with saffron & set it inne the ovene & yf you wylt hawe of foure coliurs make it as I have tawte of the tou or of the tothere.

(English, XV c.)\n[b]Cewe de Kounsye[/b]\nTak beef & hew it samal scher it & do it to the feyr & grynd garlic & do ther to & of the best spices & grynd bred & ly et in the maner of noumbles do to salt & qwan it is wellyd do it from the fyer.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Farsure of Wych[/b]\nTak fys[che] [al as?] beste and yelkys of eyren soden & saffron gynd eyren raw & bred poudre & sugre as be farse.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Tarts of Flesch[/b]\nTak fleysch of capouns or of hennys & pork & fyggys & reysings & eyren hard soden wel gronden alle to gidre brod & raw eyren do to saffron & pouder of ginger & canel and galingale & sugre & do ther to clowes & maces hole than make thin cofyn & do a cours of fleysch of perterkys or of ploverys or other volatyl al hewy & nother cours of the grounde mete & menge it togider.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Mawmene[/b]\nTak a pond of sugre & a qwart of water & an half & do it in a pot with sugre & tak amydoun & lye it ther with & tak a tendre chese & grynd it in a morter & tempre it up with almounde melk & do it in a pot & set it on the fyer & styre it wele & tak fleysch of chykenys & hew & grynd it & tempre it up with almaunde melk wel thykke & qwan thi pot is wel boylled tak it of the fyer & lye it up with fleysch & do ther to god poudre of ginger or of canel & wyth grece & dresse it & plant it.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Browet of Sarasynes[/b]\nTak crustes of qwyt bred & blood & do it in a morter & grynd it & tempre it with swet broth & draw it thorow a cloth & do it in a pot & do ther in red wyn set it on the fyer & lye it & boylle it tak perterkes & wodekokes & other smale brydes & rost hem & qwirter hem & do hem in a pot & do ther to god poudre of clowes & qwybybes & sugre & sethz it do ther in wyth grece & tast it & dresse it.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Browet Seche[/b]\nTak capouns or conyes & hew hem on gobets & waysch hem & do hem in a pot tak persoly & sauge & onyons & hew hem alle to gidre do it in a pot & red wyne & switch broth half of the ton & half of the tother & do it in the pot so that the fleysch be twey fynger brede above the pot & do ther to hol saffron & bylle it wel that non brethz go outh & set on the fyer & do ther to wyth gres & good poudere of galyngale clowes & qwybibes & let it sethen anow than do ther in sugre & dresse it.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Browet Ingse[/b]\nTak good galentyn & tempre it up weth broth & drawe it thow a fayer cloth do it in a pot & set it on the fyer. Tak qwayles & yonge pertrikes & qwarter hem & do hem in a pot & set the pot on the fyer & stire it wel & do ther in good pouder of galentyn & wyth gres & clowes & qwybibes & let it se then tyl the fleys is sodden anow tak it than of the fyer & dresse it & pouder it with sugre & maces.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Blaunch Desorre[/b]\nMak gode melk of swete almaundes & skerve the rys & do hem in a morter & grynd hem & tempre hem up with almaunde melk & draw it thorow a cloth & do it in a pot & set it on the fyer & stire it wel tak braun of capouns & do awey the skyn & the bonys & hewe it & grynd it & tempre it up with wyn & wan thi pot hayth wel boylled do ther inne of wyth ginger & tak it fro the fyer & lye it with grounde fleysch & do ther inne qwyth salt & sugre & tast it & loke that it be owerte of savour & poynaunt of the wyth ginger & loke that the thre savours a cor den ilk with othyr & dresse it & plante it with poumgarnett & gelofres.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Freschure[/b]\nTak the hert & the lyver & the blood of the hydes & sethz hem & hewe hem in a pot & do ther to qwyth gres & frye it & tak the blood & grynd it in a morter & tempre it up with red wyn & do it in the pot & tak myed bred & grynd it & tempre it up with aly tyl swet broth & lye it ther with wel chargeaunt & do ther inne good pouder & sugre florysch & serve it forth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Apilmows de Gesse[/b]\nTak apyllys & seth hem & grynd hem & drawe hem thorow a cloth & do hem in a pot & do ther to melk of almaunds & set it on the fyer & qwan it is boylled do ther to a good perty of wyth gres & loke that thu have many yelkys of eyren & do ther to in a good perty of sugre colour it with saffron dresse it & poudre it with sugre.
(English, XV c.)\n[b](untitled)[/b]\nTak freysch pork hew it & grynd it smal tak yelkys of eyren grind hem & do ther to good ginger galingale do ther to tak maces & qwybibes & clowes do ther to al hole & sugre & poudre gret plente than ley in the cofyn a smal couche of farsure tak perterkes & chikenys & hew hem on qwarter & frye hem & smale bryddys al hole fryed and conyes & do ther to a good bundel of fleysch than ley on farsure a nother good couche & do therin & do ther in greyn de parys & qwybibes & clowes & est ley a nother couche of farsure cvre it with past colour it wyt yelkys of eyren.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]A Tarte Pernusames[/b]\nTak fresch pork & sethz it  & do awey the skyn & the bonys & grynd it in a morter tak good chese & cyy it & tempre al to gidre than tempre it with eyren do therinne almaund fryede & good poudre of galingale & clowes & qwybibes & sugre & salt & saffron & reysings with out thu pepynes & grynd al to gidre tak perterkes & ploveres & wodekokes & other smale brydds tak conyes & kerwe hem & frye hem as was forseyd & farse thi dat & mak dow & couche the tarte thus ferst ley at the than aftyr ley thi farse & ley a perty of flesch ther inne & than qwibebes & sugre & good poudre reysings & dats & pumbys & damacyns & fryed almaunds ley al this in the tarte & ley thin oth couche on thi farse colour it with saffron mak thin lowes & set it in the ovene.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]A Tarte of Fysche[/b]\nTak figgs & waysch hem & grynd hem smal tempre hem with vinegre tak freysch samoun haddokes perches & pykes tak out the bonys bray hem to gidre in a morter tak poudre of ginger & galingale & meng with al tak maces & qwybibes & clowes & do ther to al hole & sugre gret plente tak ther of & do in thi cofyn a smal couche tak elys & lamprouns and frye hem to gidre in oyle de oyle & lay ther in a couche of the brayed mete & do ther to botre of almaunde melk covere it with past colour it with inne & with outen.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Charlet[/b]\nTak swete melk & colour it with saffron tak freysch pork soden hewe it smal sweng eyren & cast alm the melk set it over the fyer boille it stere it wel to gider kele it with a lytyl ale & set it doun.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Ravioles[/b]\nTak freysch pork & braun of hennys grind it smal yelks of eyren & grind hem & do ther to good poudre of maces qwybibes & mong with alwynd it in past & set it in a panne of fat broth colour it with saffron & florysch hem with hole chese gratyd.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Jussele[/b]\nMye wastelbred swenge eyren & do ther to tak good fat broth of freysch beof colour it with saffron boille it al softely & in the boyllingg do al this ther to & do to sauge & percyle.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Bokenande[/b]\nTak almaunde melk colour it with saffron forse it with good poudre tak fat fleysch wel soden hew on smale gobets do ther to lye it with amydon or with bake flour boille it set it don florysch it with poudre.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Blaunde Sorre[/b]\nTak rys & wasch hem & grynd hem smal tempre hem up with almaunde melk do it ovre the fyer & boylle it tak braun of hennys & of capouns hew it & grynd it smal as myed bred do ther to seson it with sugre gret plente florysch it with fryed almaunds.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Rosee[/b]\nTak flour of rys tempre it with almaunde melke lye it tyl it be chargeaunt tak braun of caponys or of hennys hew it & grynd it smal charge it with al colour it with alysaundre or with blood force it with clowes & maces seson it with sugre gret plente.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Ynde de Cypres[/b]\nIt sal ben mad as blaunde sorre save the colour sal ben of ynde bandas or of the flour of the violet.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Letlardes[/b]\nTak eryn & cow melk & swenge hem to gidre tak lard of freysch pork & sithen schere it on smale pecys kast it ther in hoylle & styr it tyl it be gaderyd on a crudde than leche it & kest it on a grederne & serve it with frotours.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Botre of Almaunde Melk[/b]\nTak thykke almaunde melk boyle it & in the boylinge kast ther in vinegre or vin do it sethen on a canwaas abred gadre it sethen on an keep than hange it up on a cloth amylewey wyle ley it after in a cold water than serve it forth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Charlet Aforce[/b]\nTak cow melk & eyren & swenge hem to gidre & colour it with saffron tak freysch pork hew it smal do it ther to kast it in a panne boyle it wel & stire it vyn & with ale set it don than ley it on a canwas presse out the wyth tak almaunde melk colour it with saffron lye it with amydon force it with poudre of ginger & galingale.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Farsure[/b]\nTak freysch pork soden hew it smal tak yelkes of eren & meng with al force it with poudre swete it with sugre do ther to maces qwibebis & clowes al hole colour it with saffron do it in the chykennys than boyle hem & tak hem up rost hem with gres if it be nede.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Farsure For Soper[/b]\nTak hard eyren soden & hew hem smal tak percyle & sauge & hew it smal do ther to & do it in the chikenys.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Char de Marchaunt[/b]\nTak good moton hew it on gobets & set it in a pot tak brod peper & percely grynd hem to gider tempre hem up with bred than do ther to salt & welle it.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Powmes Dorre[/b]\nTak good farsure & mak balles do hem in a panne of clene water boyle hem alityl tyl they begynng to swelle than tak hem up & ley hem on a boord to dreyen tak yelkes of eyren of swenge hem wel ther inne & let hem dreyen do hem on a spite & rost hem & in the rostinge powre on the yelkys of eyren flawme hem with grees serve hem forth with frytur.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Brewet Sechz[/b]\nHew moton & chykenys on morcellis & sethz hem with onyons & percely.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Brewet of Elys[/b]\nLye it with bred force it with poudre colour it with saffron.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Browet of Lamprouns[/b]\nLye it with bred force it with poudre of peper & galingale.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Perre[/b]\nDraw soden perys thorow a sarce so hem in a vessel to freysch broth tak sugre & hony & do ther to freysch gres tak of capouns & of hennys grynd saml & meng with al kepe it wel fro brennyng kele it & lye it charge it with yelkys of eyren.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Maumene[/b]\nTak fyggys & reysings & lese hem & grind hem & good melk of almaundys & braun of capouns & of hennys nouth outhr in yche grounden for that sal ben the colour than do there to ginger clowes gelofres & greyn de parys & sugre & salt.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Kokeneye[/b]\nTak fleysch of hennys & of capouns & lene of pork & hew the ton with the tother & onyons mynced in the broth
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Furmenty[/b]\nNym clene wete & bray it in a morter wel, þat þe holys gon al of, & seyt yt til yt breste; & nym yt vp & lat it kele. And nym fayre fresch broþ & swete mylk of almandys or swete mylk of kyne and temper yt al. & nym þe ȝolkys of eyryn & saffron & do þerto. Boyle it a lityl & set yt adoun, & messe yt forþe wyþ fat venysoun & fresch motoun.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Pise of Almayne[/b]\nNym wyte pisyn & wasch hem & seþ hem a god wyle; siþþyn wasch hem in cold watyr vnto þe holys gon of alle, and do hem alle in a pot, & keuer yt wel þat no breþ passe owt, & boyle hem ryȝt wel. & do þereto god mylk of almandys & a party of flowr of rys, & salt & safroun, & messe yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Cranys & herons[/b]\nCranys & herons schulle be enarmud wyþ lardons of swyne & rostyd & etyn wyþ gyngyuyr.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Pecokys and pertrigchis[/b]\nPecokys and pertrigchis schul ben yperboyld & lardyd & rosted & etyn wyþ gyngeuyr.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Mortrellus[/b]\nNym hennyn & porke & seþ hem togedere. Nym þe lyre of þe hennyn & þe porke & hakke smal, & grynd hit al to dust, and wyte bred þerewyþ; & temper it wyþ þe selue broþ and wyþ heyryn. And colure it wyþ safroun & boyle it, & disch it, & cast þereon powder of peper & of gyngyuyr & serue it forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Caponys in concys[/b]\nCaponys in concys schal be sodyn. Nym þe lyre & brek it smal in a morter, & peper & wyte bred þerwyþ, & temper it wyþ ale, & ley it wyþ þe capoun. Nym hard sodyn eyryn & hew þe wyte smal, & keste þereto, & nym þe ȝolkys al hole & do hem in a dysch; & boyle þe capoun & colowre it wyþ safroun, & salt it, & messe it forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Hennys in bruet[/b]\nHennys in bruet schullyn be schaldyd & sodyn wyþ porke; & grynd pepyr & comyn, bred & ale, & temper it wyþ þe selue broþ & boyle it, & colowre it wyþ safroun & salt it, & mes it forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Harys in ciuee[/b]\nHarys in ciuee schul be perboyled & lardyd & rostid; & nym onyons & myce hem ryȝt smal & fry hem in wyte gres, & grynd peper, bred, & ale, and þe onions þereto, and boyll it, & do þerto & coloure it wyþ safroun & salt it, & serue it forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Haris in talbotays[/b]\nHaris in talbotays schul be hewe in gobettys al raw and sodyn with al þe blod. Nym bred, piper & ale & grynd togedere, & temper it wyþ þe selue broth, & boyle it & salt it & serue it forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Conynggys in grauey[/b]\nConnyngys in grauey schul be sodyn & hakkyd in gobettys; and grynd gyngyuyr, galyngale & canel, & temper it vp wyþ god almand mylk & boyle it. & nym macys and clowys and kest þerin, & þe conynggis also, & salt hym & serue it forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Colys[/b]\nNym hennys & schald hem wel, & seþ hem after; & nym þe lyre & hak yt smal & bray it wyþ otyn grotys in a morter, & with wyte bred, & temper it vp wyþ þe brorth. Nym þe grete bonys & mak it þorw a cloþe, & boyle it & serue it forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Nombles[/b]\nNym þe nomblys of þe venysoun & wasch hem clene in water and salt hem, & seþ hem in tweye waterys. Grynd pepyr, bred & ale & temper it wyþ þe secunde broþe, & boyle it, & hak þe nomblys & do þeryn & serue it forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Blanche brewet de Almayne[/b]\nNym kedys or chekenys & hew hem in morsellys & seþ hem in almande mylk or in kyne mylke. Grynd gyngyuer, galingale, and cast þereto & boyle it and serue it forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Blomanger[/b]\nNym rys & lese hem & wasch hem clene, & do þereto god almande mylke & seþ hem tyl þey al tobrest; & þan lat hem kele. & nym þe lyre of þe hennyn or of capouns & grynd hem smal; kest þereto wite grese & boyle it. Nym blanchyd almandys & safroun & set hem aboue in þe dysche & serue yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Fronchemoyle[/b]\nNym eyryn wyþ al þe wyte & myse bred & schepys talwe as gret as dysys. Grynd peper and safroun and kast þerto, & do hit in þe schepis wombe. Seþ it wel & dresse it forþe of brode leches þynne.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Brynewes[/b]\nNym þe þarmys of a pygge & wasch hem clene in water & salt, & seþ hem wel; & þan hak hem smale, & grynd pepyr and safroun, bred & ale, & boyle togedere. Nym wytys of eyryn & knede it wyþ flour, & mak smal pelotys & fry hem wyþ wyte grees, & do hem in dysches aboue þat oþere mete & serue yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Appulmos[/b]\nNym appelyn & seþ hem, & lat hem kele, & mak hem þorw a cloþe. & on flesch dayes kast þereto god fat broyt of bef & god wyte grees, & sugur & safroun; and god almande mylk on fysch dayes, oyle de olyue & gode powdres; & serue it forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Froys[/b]\nNym veel and seþ yt wel & hak it smal, & grynd bred, peper & safroun and do þereto & frye yt, & presse yt wel vpon a bord, & dresse yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Fruturs[/b]\nNym flowre & eyryn & grynd peper & safroun & mak þereto a batour; & par aplyn & kyt hem to brode penys, & kest hem þereyn, & fry hem in þe batour wyþ fresch grees & serue yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Charlet[/b]\nNym porke & seþ it wel & hak yt smal. Nym eyryn wyþ al þe wytys and swyng hem wel al togedere, & kast god swete mylke þereto & boyle yt & messe yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Iussel[/b]\nNym eyryn wyþ al þe wytys & mice bred; grynd pepyr & safroun and do þereto, and temper yt wyþ god fresch broth of porke and boyle it wel, & messe yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Gees in hochepot[/b]\nNym and schald hem wel, & hewe hem wel in gobettys al rawe; & seþ hem in her owyn grees, & cast þerto wyn or ale a cuppe ful; & myce onyons smal and do þereto & boyle yt & salt yt & messe yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Eyren in bruet[/b]\nNym water & welle yt, & brek eyryn & kast þeryn, and grynd peper & safroun & temper vp wyþ swete mylk, & boyle it; & hakke chese smal & cast þeryn, & messe yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Craytoun[/b]\nTak checonys & schald hem, & seþ hem; & grynd gyngeuer oþer pepyr & comyn, and temper it vp wyþ god mylk & do þe checonys þereyn, & boyle hem & serue yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Mylk rost[/b]\nNym swete mylk & do yt in a panne. Nym eyryn wyþ al þe wyte & swyng hem wel & cast þereto & colowre yt wyþ safroun & boyle yt tyl yt wexe þykke, & þanne seyz yt þorw a culdore, & nym þat leuyþ & presse yt vpon a bord; & wan yt ys cold larde it, & scher yt on schyuerys, & roste yt on a grydern & serue yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Cryspys[/b]\nNym flour & wytys of eyryn, sugur oþer hony, & swyng togedere & mak a batour. Nym wyte grees & do yt in a posnet, & cast þe batur þereyn & stury to þou haue many; & tak hem vp & messe hem wyþ þe frutours & serue forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Berandyles[/b]\nNym hennys & seþ hem wyþ god buf, & wan hi ben sodyn nym þe hennyn & do awey þe bonys & bray smal yn a morter, & temper yt wyþ þe broth & seyz yt þorw a culdore, & cast þereto powder of gyngeuyr & sugur & graynys of powmys gernatys, & boyle yt & dresse yt in dysches, & cast aboue clowys gylofres & maces & god powder & serue yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Capons in casselys[/b]\nNym caponys & schald hem. Nym a penne & opyn þe sckyn at þe heuyd & blowe hem tyl þe sckyn ryse from þe flesche, & do of þe skyn al hole. & seþ þe lyre of hennyn & ȝolkys of heyryn & god powder, & make a farsure, & fil ful þe skyn and perboyle yt, & do yt on a spete & rost yt and droppe yt wyþ ȝolkes of eyryn & god powder rostyng. & nym þe caponys body & larde yt, & roste it, & nym almaunde mylk and amydoun and mak a batur, & droppe þe body rostyng, & serue yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Blank de surry[/b]\nTak braun of caponys oþer of hennys and þe þyes wyþowte þe skyn, & kerf hem smal als þou mayst & grynd hem smal in a morter. & tak mylk of almaundys & do yn þe braune, & grynd hem þanne togedere & seþ hem togedere. And tak flour of rys oþer amydoun and lye it þat yt be charchant, and do þereto sugur a god perti and a perty of wyt grees and boyle yt; & wan yt ys doun in dyschis straw vpon blanke poudere, and do togedere blank de sury & maumene in a dysch & serue yt forþe.

(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Maumene[/b]\nTak þe þyys oþer þe flesch of þe caponys. Seþe hem & kerf hem smal into a morter & tak mylk of almandys wyþ broth of fresch buf, & do þe flesch in þe mylk or in þe broth & do yt to þe fyre, & myng yt togedere wyþ flour of rys oþere of wastelys als charchant als þe Blank de Sure, & wyþ þe ȝolkys of eyryn for to make yt ȝolow, & safroun. & wan yt ys dressyd in dysches wyþ Blank de Sure, straw vpon clowys of gelofre & straw vpon powdre of galentyn, & serue yt forþe.

(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Bruet of Almayne[/b]\nTak pertrichys rostyd and checonys & quaylis rostyd & larkys ywol, & demembre þe oþer; & mak a god cawdel, & dresse þe flesch in a dysch & strawe powder of galentyn þervpon. Styk vpon clowys of gelofre & serue yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Bruet of Lombardye[/b]\nTak chekenys or hennys or oþere flesch, & mak þe colowre als red as any blod; & tak peper and kanel & gyngyuer bred & grynd hem in a morter, & a porcioun of bred. And mak þat bruet þenne, & do þat flesch in þat broth & mak hem boyle togedere, & stury it wel. & tak eggys & temper hem wyþ ius of percyle & wryng hem þorwe a cloþ, & wan þat bruet ys boylyd do þat þereto & meng þam togedere wyþ fayr grees so þat yt be fat ynow, & serue yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Blomanger[/b]\nDo ris in water al nyȝt & vpon þe morwe wasch hem wel & do hem vpon þe fyre for to þey breke, & noȝt for to muche; & tak braun of caponis sodyn & wel ydrawe & smal, & tak almaund mylk & boyle it wel wyþ ris, & wan it is yboylyd do þe flesch þerein so þat it be charghaunt. & do þereto a god perty of sugure, & wan it ys dressyd forþ in dischis straw þereon blaunche pouder & strik þereon almaundys fryed wyt wyte grece & serue yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Sandale[/b]\nFor to make sandale þat is perty to blomanger, tak flesch of caponys & of pork, sodyn. Kerf yt smal into a morter togedere & bray þat wel, & temper it vp wyþ broþ of caponys & of pork þat yt be wel charchaunt als þe crem of almaundys. & grynd egges and safroun or sandres togedere þat it be colourd, & straw vpon powder of galentyn, & strik þereon clowys & maces & serue it forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Apulmose[/b]\nTak applys & seþ hem and let hem kele, & after mak hem þorwe a cloþ & do hem in a pot. & kast to þat mylk of almaundys, wyþ god broþ of buf in flesch dayes; do bred ymyed þereto. & þe fisch dayes, do þereto oyle of olyue, & do þereto sugur & coloure it wyth safroun, & strew þeron powder & serue it forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Mete gelee[/b]\nFor to make mete gelee þat it be wel chariaunt, tak wyte wyn & a perty of water & safroun & gode spicis & flesch of piggys or of hennys, or fresch fisch, & boyle þam togedere; & after, wan yt ys boylyd & cold, dres yt in dischis & serue yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Murrey[/b]\nTak mulbery & bray hem in a morter & wryng hem þorh a cloþ, & do hem in a pot ouer þe fyre; & do þereto bred & wyte gresse, & let yt naȝt boyle non ofter þan onys. & do þereto a god perty of sugur, & ȝif yt be noȝt ynowe ycolowrd brey mulburus; & serue yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Pench of egges[/b]\nTak water & do it in a panne to þe fyre, & lat yt sethe; & after tak egges & brek hem & cast hem in þe water. & after tak a chese & kerf yt on fowre pertis & kast in þe water, & wanne þe chese and þe eggys ben wel sodyn, tak hem owt of þe water & wasch hem in clene water. & tak wastel breed & temper yt wyþ mylk of a kow, & after do yt ouer þe fyre, & after forsy yt wyþ gyngeuer and wyþ comyn & colowre yt wyþ safroun, & lye yt wyþ eggys. & oyle þe sewe wyþ boter, & kep wel þe chese owt, & dresse þe sewe & do þin eggys þereon al ful, & kerf þy chese in lytyl schyuis & do hem in þe sewe wyþ eggys, and serue yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Comyn[/b]\nTak god almaunde mylk & lat yt boyle, & do þerein amydoun wyþ flowre of rys, & colowre yt wyþ safroun; & after dresse yt wyþ greynis of poum garnettes oþer wyþ reysyns, ȝyf þow hast non oþer. & tak sugur & do þereyn & serue yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Fruturs[/b]\nTak crommys of wyte bred & þe flowris of þe swete appyl tre and ȝolkys of eggys, and bray hem togedere in a morter, and temper it vp wyþ wyte wyn and make yt to seþe. & wan yt ys þykke do þereto god spicis of gyngeuer, galyngale, canel, and clowys gelofre, and serue yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Rosee[/b]\nTak þe flowrys of rosys and wasch hem wel in water, and after bray hem wel in a morter; & þan tak almondys and temper hem, & seþ hem. & after tak flesch of capons or of hennys and hac yt smale, & þan bray hem wel in a morter, & þan do yt in þe rose so þat þe flesch acorde wyþ þe mylk, & so þat þe mete be charchaunt; & after do yt to þe fyre to boyle, & do þereto sugur & safroun þat yt be wel ycolowrd & rosy of leuys of þe forseyde flowrys, & serue yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Pommedorry[/b]\nTak buff & hewe yt smal al raw, & cast yt in a morter & grynd yt noȝt to smal. Tak safroun & grynd þerewyþ. Wan yt ys grounde, tak þe wyte of þe eyryn, ȝyf yt be noȝt styf; cast into þe buf pouder of pepyr, olde reysyns & reysyns of coronse. Set ouer a panne wyþ fayr water, & mak pelotys of þe buf; & wan þe water & þe pelotes ys wel yboylyd, set yt adoun & kele yt. Put yt on a broche & rost yt, & endorre yt wyþ ȝolkys of eyryn & serue yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Longe de buf[/b]\nNym þe tonge of þe rether & schalde, & schawe yt wel & ryȝt clene, & seth yt; & seþe nym a broche, & larde yt wyþ lardons and wyþ clowys gelofre, & do it rostyng. & drop yt, wel yrostyd, wyþ ȝolkys of eyrin, & dresse it forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Rew de runsy[/b]\nNym swynys fet & eyr & make hem clene, & seth hem half wyþ wyn & half wyþ water. Cast mycyd onyons þereto & god spicis, & wan þey be ysodyn nym & rosty hem on a grydere. Wan it is yrostyd kest þereto of þe selue broth ylyed wyþ amydoun and amycyd onyons, & serue yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Bukkenade[/b]\nNym god fresch flesch, wat maner so yt be, & hew yt in smale morselys, & seth yt wyþ gode fresch buf; & cast þereto gode myncyd onyons & gode spicerye, & alyth wyþ eyryn, & boyle & dresse yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Spine[/b]\nNym þe flowrys of þe hawþorn clene gaderyd & bray hem al to dust, & temper hem wyþ almaunde mylk & aly yt wyþ amydoun & wyþ eyryn wel þykke; & boyle it & messe yt forth, & flowrys & leuys abouyn on.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Rosee & Fresee & Swau[/b]\nRosee & fresee & swau: þey schal be ymad in þe selue maner.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Mortrellus blanc[/b]\nNym pyggus and hennys & oþer maner fresch flesch & hew yt in morselys & seth yt in wyth wyn, & nym gyngyuer & galyngale & gelofre & canel, & bray yt wel & kest þerto. & alye yt wyþ amydoun oþer wyþ flowr of rys.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Amendement for mete þat ys to salt, & ouer mychyl[/b]\nNym ote mele & bynd yt in a fayr lynnyn clowt, & lat yt honge in þe pot so þat yt towche noȝt þe bottym, & lat yt hongy þereynne a god wyle; & seþe set yt fro þe fyre & let yt kele, & yt schal be fresch ynow wyþoute any oþer maner licowr ydo þereto.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Rapy[/b]\nTak fygys & reysyns & wyn, & grynd hem togeder; tak and draw hem þorw a cloþ & do þereto powdere of alkenet oþer of rys. & do þereto a god quantite of powder of pepir & vyneger, and boyle it togedere, & messe yt & serue yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Egge dows[/b]\nTak almaundys & mak god mylk, & temper wyþ god wyneger clene. Tak reysynys & boyle hem in clene water, & tak þe reysynis & tak hem owt of þe water & boyle hem wyþ milk, & ȝyf þow wyl colowre yt wyþ safroun & serue yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Mallard in cyuey[/b]\nTak a mallard & pul hym drye, & swyng ouer þe fyre. Draw hym, but lat hym touche no water; & hew hym in gobettys, & do hym in a pot of clene water. Boyle hym wel & tak onyons & boyle, & bred & pepyr, & grynd togedere & drawe þorw a cloþ. Temper wyþ wyn, & boyle yt, & serue yt forþ.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Bukkenade[/b]\nTak veel & boyle it. Tak ȝolkys of eggys & mak hem þykke. Tak macis & powdre of gyngyuer & powdere of peper, & boyle yt togedere & messe yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Roo broth[/b]\nTak persile & ysop & sauge, & hak yt smal. Boil it in wyn & in water & a lytyl powdre of peper & messe yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Bruet of sarcynesse[/b]\nTak þe lyre of þe fresch buf & ket it al in pecis, & bred, & fry yt in fresch gres. Tak it vp & drye it, & do yt in a vessel wyþ wyn & sugur & powdre of clowys. Boyl yt togedere tyl þe flesch haue drong þe lycoure, & tak almande mylk & quibibz, macis & clowys, & boyle hem togedere. Tak þe flesch & do þereto & messe it forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Gely[/b]\nTak hoggys fet oþer pyggys, oþer erys, oþer pertrichys oþere chiconys, & do hem togedere & seth hem in a pot; & do in hem flowre of canel and clowys hole or grounde. Do þereto vineger, & tak & do þe broth in a clene vessel of al þys, & tak þe flesch and kerf yt in smale morselys & do yt þerein. Tak powder of galyngale & cast aboue & lat yt kele. Tak bronchys of þe lorere tre & styk ouer it, & kep yt al so longe as þou wilt & serue yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]To kepe venisoun fro restyng[/b]\nTak venisoun wan yt ys newe & cuuer it hastely wyþ fern þat no wynd may come þereto and wan þou hast ycuuer yt wel led yt hom & do yt in a soler þat sonne ne wynd may come þerto. & dimembre it, & do yt in a clene water & lef yt þere half a day, and after do yt vpon herdeles for to dre; & wan yt ys drye tak salt, & do after þy venisoun axit, & do yt boyle in water þat be so salt als water of þe see and moche more. & after lat þe water be cold, þat it be þynne, & þanne do þy venisoun in þe water & lat yt be þerein þre daies & þre nyȝt; & after tak yt owt of þe water & salt it wyþ dre salt ryȝt wel in a barel, & wan þy barel ys ful cuuer it hastely þat sunne ne wynd come þereto.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]To do awey restyng of venisoun[/b]\nTak þe venisoun þat ys rest & do yt in cold water & after mak an hole in þe herþe & lat yt be þereyn þre dayes & þre nyȝt; & after tak yt vp & frot yt wel wyþ gret salt of poite þere were þe restyng ys. & after lat yt hange in reyn water al nyȝt or more.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Poum dorroge[/b]\nTak pertrichis wit longe filettis of pork al raw & hak hem wel smale, and after bray hem in a morter. & wan þey be wel brayd do þereto god plente of poudere & ȝolkys of eyryn. & after mak þereof a farsure formed of þe gretnesse of a onyoun, & after do it boyle in god breth of buf oþer of pork. After lat yt kele, & after do it on a broche of hasel & do hem to þe fere to roste. & after mak god bature of floure & egges, on bature wyt & an oþere ȝelow & do þereto god plente of sugur & tak a feþere or a styk & tak of þe bature & peynte þereon aboue þe applyn so þat on be wyt & þat oþere ȝelow wel colourd.
(English, XIV c.)\n
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Egerduse[/b]\nTak lucys or tenchis & hak hem smal in gobettes, & fry hem in oyle de oliue; & syþ nym vineger & þe þredde perty of sugur & myncyd onyons smal, & boyle al togedere, & cast þereyn clowys, macys & quibibz & serue yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Rapy[/b]\nTak pykes or tenchis or oþere maner fresch fysch & fry yt wyþ oyle de oliue, & syþ nym þe crustys of wyt bred & canel & bray it al wel in a mortere, & temper yt vp wyþ god wyn & cole yt þorw an hersyue, & loke þat yt be al ycoloured of canel; & boyle yt, & cast þerein hole clowys & macys & quibibz, & do þe fysch in dischis & rape abouyn, & dresse yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Fygey[/b]\nNym figes & boille hem in wyn, and bray hem in a morter wiþ lied bred. Tempre hit vp wyþ goud wyn; boille it. Do þerto goud spicere & hole resons. Dresse hit; florisshe it aboue wiþ pomme garnetes.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Pommys morles[/b]\nNym rys & bray hem wel, & temper hem vp wyþ almaunde mylk & boyle yt. Nym applyn & pare hem & sher hem smal als dicis, & cast hem þereyn after þe boylyng, & cast sugur wyþal, & colowre yt wyþ safroun & cast þereto pouder, & serue yt forthe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Rys moyle[/b]\nNym rys & bray hem ryȝt wel in a mortere, & cast þereto god almaunde mylk & sugur & salt; & boyle it & serue yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Sowpys dorry[/b]\nNym onyons & mynce hem smale & fry hem in oyle dolyf. Nym wyn & boyle yt wyþ þe onyouns. Toste wyte bred & do yt in dischis, & god almande mylk also, & do þe wyne with onyons aboue & serue yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Blomanger of fysch[/b]\nTak a pound of rys. Les hem wel & wasch, & seþ tyl þey breste & lat hem kele; & do þereto mylk of to pound of almandys. Nym þe perche or þe lopuster & boyle yt, & kest sugur & salt also þerto, & serue yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Potage of rys[/b]\nTak rys & les hem and wasch hem clene, & seþ hem tyl þey breste, & þan lat hem kele. & seþ cast þerto almand mylk and colour it wiþ safroun, & boyle it & messe yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Lampray fresch in galentyne[/b]\nSchal be latyn blod atte nauel, and schald yt & rost yt, & ley yt al hole vpon a plater, & ȝyf hym forth wyþ galentyn þat be mad of galyngale, gyngeuer & canel, & dresse yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Salt lomprey in galentyne[/b]\nYt schal be stoppit ouer nyȝt in lewe water & in braan, & flawe, & sodyn. & pyl onyons & seþ hem & ley hem al hol by þe lomprey, & ȝif hem forþe wyþ galentyne makyþ wyþ strong wyneger & wyþ paryng of wyt bred, & boyle it al togedere & serue yt forþe.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Lampreys in bruet[/b]\nþey schulle be schaldyd & ysode & ybrulyd vpon a gredern, & grynd peper & safroun & do þerto, & boyle it & do þe lomprey þeryn & serue yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Storchoun[/b]\nHe schal be schorn in lesys & stepyd ouer nyȝt, & sodyn longe as flesch; & he schal be etyn in veneger.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Solys in bruet[/b]\nþey schal be fleyn & sodyn & rostyd vpon a gredern, & grynd peper & safroun, bred & ale; boyle it wel & do þe sole in a plater & þe bruet aboue & serue it forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Oystryn in bruet[/b]\nþey schul be schallyd & ysod in clene water. Grynd peper, safroun, bred & ale, & temper it wyþ broth. Do þe oystryn þerynne & boyle it & salt it & serue it forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Elys in bruet[/b]\nþey schul be flayn & ket in gobettes & sodyn; and grynd peper & safroun, oþer myntys & persele, & bred & ale, & temper it wyþ þe broth & boyle it & serue it forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Lopister[/b]\nTak a pound of rys. Les hem wel & wasch, & seþ tyl þey breste & lat hem kele; & do þereto mylk of to pound of almandys. Nym þe perche or þe lopuster & boyle yt, & kest sugur & salt also þerto, & serue yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Porreyne[/b]\nTak prunys fayrist. Wasch hem wel & clene & frot hem wel in a syue þat þe ius be wel ywronge, do it in a pot. & do þereto wyt gres & a perty of sugur oþer hony, & make hem to boyle togedere, & mak yt þykke wyþ flowr of rys oþer wastel bred, & wan it is sodyn dresse it into dischis & strew þeron powder & serue it forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Chireseye[/b]\nTak chiryes at þe fest of Seynt Iohn þe Baptist, & do awey þe stonys. Grynd hem in a morter, & after frot hem wel in a seue so þat þe ius be wel comyn owt; & do þan in a pot & do þerein feyre gres or boter & bred of wastel ymyid, & of sugur a god perty, & a porcioun of wyn. & wan it is wel ysodyn & ydressyd in dyschis, stik verin clowis of gilofre & strew þeron sugur.
(English, XIV c.)\n
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Blank desure[/b]\nTak þe ȝolkys of egges sodyn & temper it wyþ mylk of a kow. & do þerto comyn & safroun & flowre of ris or wastel bred myed, & grynd in a morter & temper it vp wyþ þe milk; & mak it boyle & do þerto wit of egges coruyn smal. & tak fat chese & kerf þerto wan þe licour is boylyd, & serue it forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Graue enforse[/b]\nTak triyd gyngeuer & safroun & grynd hem in a morter & temper hem vp wyþ almandys, & do hem to þe fire; & wan it boylyþ wel do þerto ȝolkys of egges sodyn & fat chese coruyn in gobettis. & wan it is dressid in dischis, strawe vpon powder of galyngale & serue it forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Hony douse[/b]\nTak god mylk of almandys & rys, & wasch hem wel in a feyre vessel & in fayre hot water. & after do hem in a feyre towayl for to drie, & wan þat þey be drye bray hem wel in a morter al to flowre; & after bet hem togedere. & afterward tak two pertyis & do þe half in a pot & þat oþer half in a noþer pot, & colowr þat on wyþ þe safroun & lat þat oþer be wyt. & lat yt boyle tyl it be þykke, & do þerto a god perty of sugur, & after dresse yt in two dischis; & loke þat þou haue almandys boylid in water & in safroun & in wyn, & after frie hem & set hem vpon þe forseyde mete, & strew þeron sugur þat yt be wel ycolouryt & serue yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Potage fene boiles[/b]\nTak wite benes & seþ hem in water, & bray þe benys in a morter al to noȝt; & lat hem seþe in almande mylk & do þerein wyn & hony. & seþ reysouns in wyn & do þerto & after dresse yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Tartys in applis[/b]\nTak gode applys & gode spycis & figys & reysons & perys, & wan þey arn wel ybrayd colour wyþ safroun wel & do yt in a cofyn, & do yt forth to bake wel.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Rys alkere[/b]\nTak figys & reysons, & do awey þe kernelis; & a god perty of applys, & do awey þe paryng of þe applis & þe kernelis; & bray hem wel in a morter & temper hem vp wyþ almande mylk & menge hem wyþ flour of rys þat yt be wel chariand. & strew þervpon powder of galyngale & serue yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Tartys of fysch owt of lente[/b]\nMake þe cowche of fat chese & gyngeuer & canel & pure creym of mylk of a kow & of helys ysoden, & grynd hem wel wyþ safroun; & mak þe cowche of canel & of clowys & of rys & of gode spycys as oþer tartys fallyþ to be.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Morrey[/b]\nFor to make morrey, require de carnibus vt supra
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Flownys in lente[/b]\nTak god flowr & make a god past; & tak god mylk of almandys & flowr of rys oþer of amydoun & boyle hem togedere þat þey be wel chariand. Wan yt is boylid þykke take yt vp & ley yt on a feyre bord so þat yt be cold, & wan þe cofyns ben makyd tak a perty & do vpon þe coffyns, & kerf hem in schiueris; & do in hem god mylk of almandys & figys & datys & kerf yt in fowre pertyis, & do yt to bake & serue yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Rapee[/b]\nTak þe crustys of wyt bred & reysons & bray hem wel in a morter, & after temper hem vp wyþ wyn & wryng hem þorw a cloþ. & do þereto canel, þat yt be al colouryt of canel, & do þereto hole clowys, macys & quibibz. þe fysch schal be lucys oþer tenchis fryid, or oþer maner fysch so þat yt be fresch and wel yfryid; & do yt in dischis, & þat rape vpon, & serue yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Porrey chapeleyn[/b]\nTak an hundred onyons oþer an half, & tak oyle de olyf & boyle togedere in a pot; & tak almande mylk & boyle yt & do þereto. Tak & make a þynne paast of dow, & make þerof as it were ryngis. Tak & fry hem in oyle de olyue or in wyte grees & boil al togedere.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Formenty on a fichssday[/b]\nTak þe mylk of þe hasel notis. Boyl þe wite wyth þe aftermelk til it be dryyd, & tak & coloure yt wyth safroun; & þe ferst mylk cast þerto & boyle wel, & serue yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Blank de syry[/b]\nTak almande mylk & flowre of rys; tak þerto sugur, & boyle þys togedere, & dische yt. & tak almandys & wet hem in water of sugur, & drye hem in a panne, & plante hem in þe mete & serue yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Pynade[/b]\nTak hony and rotys of radich & grynd yt smal in a morter, & do to þat hony a quantite of broun sugur. Tak powder of peper & safroun & almandys, & do al togedere. Boyl hem long & held yt on a wet bord & let yt kele, & messe yt & do yt forth.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Balough broth[/b]\nTak pikys & spred hem abrod, & helys, ȝif þou hast, fle hem & ket hem in gobettys; & seþ hem in half wyn & half in water. Tak vp þe pykys & elys & hold hem hote, & draw þe broth þorwe a cloþe. Do powder of gyngeuer, peper & galyngale & canel into þe broth & boyle yt, & do yt on þe pykys & on þe elys & serue yt forth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To make a stew of flesh[/b]\nTo make a stew of flesh yf thy potte be .iiij. gallons do yn A quarte of wyn take fayre befe of the fore loyne or of the hynder loyne and mynsitt and take gode Capons with all Take pepur and gode poder of Cannell and gyngere and rasyns of Corance clowse maces saferon & saunders take þer to onyons percelly sage Rosemary tyme ysope saffery hony clarefyed and a quantite of bryssyd Almondys and put ther to and boyll hit vp but thow nedys to have A fayre of colys for byrnyng And not to grete A fyre but small sokyng fyre And sokyd well in þe stewyng And loke thy pott be well keverd that the hete go not owte in no wyse And thus stew all maner flesh.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To make gode almondys mylke[/b]\nTake brokyn sugure or for fawte ther of take claryfied hony and put hit into fayre water And set hit on the fyre and boyle hit and skymme hit clene and set hit be syde the fyre and let hit cole and then blanche thy almondys cast them yn a morter and bray them small temper hem up with þe same water.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To dyght A crabe[/b]\nTake owte all yn the Crabe and lay hit yn a lityll vyneAgyr take And put A litell rede Wyne ther to and streyne all throwgh A streynner take pouder of gynger synamome and sugure and menge hem all togeder And put hym yn the shell And set hit on the fyre tyll he boyll and when hit ys boyled take hit of and cast pouder of synamome and sugure A pon and serue hit furth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For fryturs[/b]\nWith egges and flowr a bator thow make\nPut barme ther to I vnder take\nCollor hit with saferon or thow more do\nTake pouder of pepur and cast ther to\nKerve Appyls evyn A thorte cast þer yn\nFry ham in swete grece no more I myn \nCast sugur ther to yf thow be gynne
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Sauce for a mawlerd Rosted[/b]\nTake onyons And mense them wele\nPut sum yn thy mawlerd so have the sele \nAnd mynce mo Onyons I the ken \nWith the grece of the mawlerd seth hit then\nPut ale mustad And hony ther to\nBoyle all to geder tyll hit be enowe
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To make sauce for A pyke[/b]\nTake the refette of the pyke and mynse hit small and put hit yn A dyshe and take a gode mese of musterd And put of the best and fattest of þe broth a [illegible] the saucer and shakyd and put hit in to the dyshe with the refete and put yn a litell vyneAger and a lytell vergys ther to And a grete quantite of Syamom & sugure and lityll gynger and as ye fele hit with your mowth ye may all way amend hit.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For to seth a pyke[/b]\nKyll hym yn the hede styke and take a handfull of grete salt rub hym tyll the flewme goo fro hym opyn hym at the belly and take owte the refete and take oute the gall and stryppe all the small guttes and cast them a Way and save the grete gutte. Take A fayre clene panne And a quarte of fayre Water take new ale a quarte and a dyshe full of este and take ii. handefull of salt and cast ther yn Take a lityll gynger and synamom and cast þer to rosemary mageron tyme and percelly and a lityll savery and breke all thes herbes in two and cast yn the panne yf he be not Well refete cast yn a lityll suete botter but seth hit.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]A pecoke[/b]\nCut hym yn necke and skald hym cut of þe fete & hede cast hym on a spete bake hym well the sauce ys gynger.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Gurnard[/b]\nTake hym and slytte A litill the wombe And take owte the guttys and and seth hym in sauce of salte water and ale the sauce is pepur And vyneAger.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Sturgeon[/b]\nTake and lay hym in Water over nyght seth hym and let hym kele and lay hym in vyneAger or yn Aysell that sauce is kyndely ther to serue hit furth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For tarts owte of lente[/b]\nTake neshe chese and pare hit and grynd hit yn A morter and breke egges and do ther to and then put yn buttur and creme and mell all well to gethur put not to moche butter ther yn if the chese be fatte make A coffyn of dowe and close hit a bove with dowe and collor hit a bove with the yolkes of eggs and bake hit well and serue hit furth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Lamprays in brewte[/b]\nTake lawprays and skall them be kynde then roste hem on A grede yrne and grynd pepur And saferon, mell hit with Ale so serue the lamprays.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]A lopstere[/b]\nA lopster shall be bakyn yn a noven or vnder A pan by the fyre side and then ete hym with vyneager. 
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Egges yn brewte[/b]\nTake water and seth hit. in the same water breke your egges and cast ther on gynger pepur and saferon than temper hit vp with swete mylke and boile hit And then kerve chese and cast ther to small kutte And when hit ys ynowgh serue hit furth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To make colde mylke of Almoundys[/b]\nDo fayre water in a pott And do þer to brokyn suger And for faute ther of clene claryfied hony so that hit be sumdele dosett and do ther to A litill salte set hit on the fyre And when hit ys At the boylyng skeme hit clene And let hit boyle but A whyle then take hit of and let hit kele then blaunce þe Almounds and temper them vp with the same water & streyne hit And make hit A thycke mylke And put ther to A litill Wyne that hit may savor a litill þer of then toste brede & lay hit yn A whyle And then lay hit on the roste yre A gayne so that hit be harde And cowche them on A dyshe And put your mylke And serue hit furth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To make buttyrd Wortys[/b]\nTake all maner of gode herbys that ye may gette pyke them washe them and hacke them and boyle them vp in fayre water and put ther to butture clarefied A grete quantite And when they be boylde enowgh salt them but let non Ote mele come ther yn And dyse brede in small gobbetts & do hit in dyshys and powre the wortes A pon and serue hit furth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To make lyede mylke[/b]\nTake kow mylke and sugure and do them yn A pot set hit on the fyre and when hit boylls put þere to yowlkes of eggys loke that hit be rynnyng And not to charchant take white brede cut yn small soppys do them yn dyshes and powre hit there vpon. And serue hit furth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To make grewell of forse[/b]\nTake mary bones of Fresh beef And make goode grewell ther of then draw hit throwgh a streynner Take fayre porke tender sodyn take A way the skynne and the bonys and the senose Then grynde hit yn A morter small And tempyr hit vp with the same grewell that ys drawne make hit smoth let hit stand resonayll by þe flesh seson hit vp with salte and saferon then set hit to the fyre and let hit boyle And serue hit furth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To torne Wyne to Vyneagyr or Ale to Aleger or syder to Aysell[/b]\nTake a pott and fyll hit Full of wyne Asell or gode Ale And stoppe well the mowth that no thyng cum yn nor owte And do hit in A vessell full of water and set the vessell on the fyre And let the pot of wyne boyle in the same A long while tyll hit be turnyd.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To make A podyng of A nox or of A shepe[/b]\nTake the blode and swyng hit with thy hand and cast a way the lumpys that kyeneth then take sewet of the same and mynse hit small and put in to þe blode also put in plenty of otyn grytts and fyll up thy ropeys with the same and sethe them and after broyle them When they be colde And serue þem forth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To make gallentyne[/b]\nTake Crustys of white sowre brede and tost hit tyll hit be brown brynnyd and stepe hit in vynAgyre and draw hem throwgh A streynner with the same vynneAger set on the fyre And boyle hit well and cast ther yn sawnders pouder of gynger And synamom and a litell pepur And if hit be to terte put more sugar ther to And that will Amend hit.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Dowcetts[/b]\nTake past and make lityll cofyns lesse then sawsers and set them yn the oven and hardyn hem and take mary of a nox cow and goode almoundes mylk and stere them well to gethur with sugur And powder of ginger And synamome and salt and put in the Cofyns and set them yn þe oven to bake and serue hit furth all with white colours.

(English, XV c.)\n[b]The sydes of A dere of hye grece Rostyde[/b]\nWashe the sydes of A dere do A way þe fyllets do them on A broche and rost them put them on the broche Auvterwards and a payne crose wyse Take rede wyne powder of pepyr and salt and baste them ther with tyll ther be enowgh & have a charcuye under to kepe that fallys down and wash hym ther with A gayn then serve hit forth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Chekyns Farsed[/b]\nBreke the skynne At the necke behynd And blow hym that the skyn may a ryse from the flesh draw them washe hem clene and chop of the hedys. Take the lene of ffatte porke sothyn and hackyd small with rawe yolkys of eggys and harde yolkys mynsyde small and rasyns of Curance and other powders & herbys perboyled and hewd small and put yn saferon and salt do to gethur all thes and stuffe thy chekyns ther with betwene the flesh and the skyn and plumbe them in hote broth and then make them smoth with thy hands that the stuff lye evyn ondur the skyn than perboyle them a lytill then rost them And serue them furth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To make Alloes of beef[/b]\nTake lene beef and cut hym in thyn pecys and lay hit on A borde then take sewet of motton or of beef and herbys and onyons hackyd small to gether then straw thy leshes of beef with powder of pepur and a lytell salt and strew on thy sewet and the herbys. And rolle them up ther yn put them on a broche and roste them and serue them up hote.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Samon rostyd in sause[/b]\nCutte thy samon in Rownde pecys and roste hit on a roste Yre take wyne and powder of cannell and draw hem throwgh a streynner. Do ther to onyons mynsed small boyle hit well take vynegyr or verius and pouder of gynger and salt do ther to lay the samon In dyshys and pore the syrrppe ther on and serue forth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To make mortrose of Fyshe[/b]\nTake hownde fyshe haddock or codlyng seth hit and pyke hit clene fro the bonys take a way the skyn and grynde the lyver ther with blanched almounds And temper thy mylke with the broth of the fresh Fyshe and make a gode mylke of do ther to myad of white brede and sugure set hit to the fyre when hit boylys loke hit be stondyng mese serue hit furth strow on Blawnche powdyr.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To make Creme of Almoundes[/b]\nBlanche almounds kepe them As ye may them temper up to A thycke mylke with fayre water streyne hit and put hit in A pott and set hit on the fyre stere hit well when hit begynnys to ryse up take hit of yf thow have moche do ther to A dyschfull of VynAgyr yf thou have but a litell do the lesse hele the pot let hit stonde A whyle. Take a clene cloth holdyn a brode betwene .iiij. folkes streyte & cast the creme þer on with a ladyll as brode as the cloth And rubbe the cloth toward and froward with the egge of the ladyll that þer may woyde the water. Then gather hit to geder in þe myddyl of the cloth bynde the .iiij. Corners to geder and hang on A pynne that the Water may soke onto And then do hit in A bolle And tempyr hit up wyth white wyne And bete hit with a sawser on to the tyme that hit be softe.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To make Chawden for A Swan or for Wylde gose[/b]\nTake the herte of the Swanne the gysserue the wynges And fete And set hit over the fyre yn a pott wyth fayre water and draw a lyre with brede and rede wyne And put to the same And seson hit vp with powder of pepyr pouder of gynger and salt and loke hit have a goode coloure of his own blode And dresse the Chawden with the purtenante A Cordyn ther with.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Capons in dorre[/b]\nBlanched almoundes grynd hem temper them vp with fare water un to A goode mylke And draw hit through A streynenor in to A pott do ther to saferon for yf thow wylt thow may cullor hit A litill ther with And put ther to sugure and salte and set hit on the fyre stere hit well and when hit is at the boylyng do ther to A litell goode wyne take hit fro the fyre And stere hit well And then take white brede and cut hit manor of brewes thyn tost them A litell on A rost yrne that thei be sumdele brown And then dyppe hem A litell in wyne And tost hem better and do a litell mylke in dysches and coche .iij. or .iiij. tostes in A dysche And powre more mylke A pon And serue hit forth. probatu est.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Capons stewed[/b]\nTake percelly Isope sage Rosemary And tyme breke hit betwene thy hands and stoppe thy capons ther with and color them with saferon And put them yn A erthyn pot or els in brasse for erth is better. And lay splentys underneth and all a boute the sydes so that the capons tuche not the sydes nother the bottom and cast of the same herbys in to þe pot A mong the capons And put a quart or A pynte of the best wyne that thow cansye gette and no other licour And set A lydde ther A pon that wyll ly with yn the brym. And make batur of white of eggys & floure And put betwene the brym A paper lefe or els lyncloth that the batur may stop hit sowrely þat no eyre com owte loke þat hit be thyke of bature And set thy pot on A charecole fyre to the myd syde & se þat the lydde ryse not with the hette and let hit stew esely and long and whan þow supposyth hit is enowgh take hit fro the fyre yf hit be A pot of erth set hit upon a wyspe of ftraw that hit toche not the cold grownde And when the hete is well drawn and over past take of the lydde And take owte thy capons with a stycke And ley them in A noþer vessell and make A syrryp of Wyne And mynct datys and Cannell drawn with the same wyne do ther to rasyns of corance sugur safferon And salt boyle hit A litill And cast yn powder of gynger with a litell of the same wyne do the sew to the syrryppe a bove upon the capons And serue hem furth with A rybbe of beffe ever more a capon on a dysche.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For to stew heryng[/b]\nSe thy heryng be well watered and take owte the bone and take the myltys and lay them yn A fayre dysch of water and wesche both the heryng and the mylt to gether then take a litell percely so muche tyme a Fewe unyons and mell all to gether as small as ye can make hit and then bruse all your herbes and the mylts together And take poder of pepur a litell suger and rasyns of Curance and a litell myed of White brede and put all thes together and stew thy heryng with all When they be stuffed lay them on A dyshe and take ale a gode porcon and put ther to musterd and cast vpon them grete Rasyns and cover them with a dyshe and set them on þe fyre and so serue them furth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To make venegur manede;[/b]\nTake a gad of stele I wot in dede;\nIn strong venegur þou schalt hit seke\nix sythes in venegur, þerof þou reke,\nA bere with þe hete hit þou may,\nAnd in goode wyne sleck hit I say;\nHit shalle be venegur I wot hit wele,\nTo serve at a tyme at fest or mele.\nAnd rosted benes, þat steped han bene,\nGoode wyne schalle turne to venegur be dene.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To preve venegur, weþer hit be fyne.[/b]\nÞou take hys knyve or ellis myne,\nIn harde drye flore a hole to make;\nPut in þo venegur, I undurtake,\nIf hit be good, welle, syr, hit schalle,\nYf hit be noȝt, downe wylle hit falle.\nÞis seȝe I preved, so have I blys;\nÞerfore I wot þat hit sothe is.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To powder befe with in a nyȝt,[/b]\nÞou welle þo salt, in water bryȝt;\nMalt hit in bryne, set doun to kele,\nPut in þy flesshe fayre and wele,\nAnd in a nyȝt hit poudert schalle be,\nGrene powdert þorogh, so mot I þe.\nYf þy dysshe metes dere ben to salt,\nKerve a grene sod, I wot, þou schalt,\nAnd kover þy pot with þo gresse done,\nÞo salt on þo gresse shalle barke fulle sone.\nWith þy honde smyte of, I say;\nÞo salt lay on anew þou may;\nÞys schalt þou gedur hit, yche a dele,\nAnd make hit fresshe unto þe mele.\nIf I schalle of þese potage spelle\nA whyle þeron þen most I dwelle;\nFyrste, to speke of furmenté,\nHow hit is made in yche degre.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Furmente.[/b]\nTake wete, and pyke hit fayre and clene\nAnd do hit in a morter shene;\nBray hit a lytelle, with water hit spryng\nTyl hit hulle, with-oute lesyng.\nÞen wyndo hit wele, nede þou mot;\nWasshe hit fayre, put hit in pot;\nBoyle hit tylle hit brest, þen\nLet hit doun, as I þe kenne.\nTake know mylke, and play hit up\nTo hit be thykkerede to sup.\nLye hit up with ȝolkes of eyren,\nAnd kepe hit wele, lest hit berne.\nColoure hit with safron and salt hit wele,\nAnd servyd hit forthe, Syr, at þe mele;\nWith sugur candy, þou may hit dowce,\nIf hit be served in grete lordys howce.\nTake black sugur for mener menne;\nBe ware þer with, for hit wylle brenne.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Amydone.[/b]\nTake wete and stepe hit dayes ix;\nÞus chaunge þy water yche day be dene.\nBrys hit in a morter ryȝt smalle,\nSethe hit with mylke and water with alle.\nÞorowgh a herseve loke þou hit sye,\nAnd let hit stonde and setel bye;\nPoure oute þe water, in clothe hit lay,\nTyl hit be drye þou turne hit ay.\nÞys is a lycour as men sayn,\nÞer of I schalle speke more in playn.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Conyngus in gravé.[/b]\nSethe welle þy conyngus in water clere,\nAfter, in water colde þou wasshe hom sere,\nTake mylke of almondes, lay hit anone\nWith myed bred or amydone;\nFors hit with cloves or gode gyngere;\nBoyle hit over þo fyre,\nHew þo conyngus, do hom þer to,\nSeson hit with wyn or sugur þo.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Chekyns in cretene.[/b]\nTake cow mylke, lye hit anone\nWith flowre, or ellis with amydone;\nFors hit with galyngale and gode gyngere,\nWith canel and comyn, alle in fere,\nColoure hit with safron þo;\nÞe chekyns by hom selfe þo sethe þer to,\nHew hom in quarteres and lay hom inne,\nBoyle hom up with alle, no more ne mynne;\nBut seson hit with sugur suete,\nAnd serve hom forthe for þay ben sete
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Viande de Cipur.[/b]\nTake braunne of capons or hennes þou shalle;\nParboyle and drye hit with alle;\nHew hom smalle, bray in mortere,\nAs smalle as bred, þat myed were;\nTake good almonde mylke anone\nAnd lye hit up with amydone\nOr with floure of ryse, þou may;\nColoure hit with safron, I þe say;\nBoyle hit after yche adele,\nCharge hit with flesshe brayed wele;\nSeson hit with sugur and þen þy dysshe\nWith almondes set þou schalle florysshe.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Mortrews de chare.[/b]\nTake hennes and fresshe porke, y þe kenne,\nSethe hom togedur alwayes þenne;\nTake hem up, pyke out þe bonys,\nEnbande þe porke, Syr, for þo nonys;\nHew hit smalle and grynde hit wele,\nCast it agayne, so have þou cele,\nIn to þe brothe, and charge hit þenne\nWith myed wastelle, as I þe kenne;\nColour hit with safron, at þat tyde;\nBoyle hit and set hit doune be syde;\nLye hit with ȝolkes of eren ryȝt,\nAnd florysshe þy dysshe with pouder þou myȝt.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Blonc Manger.[/b]\nTake ryse and loke þou wasshe hom clene,\nAnd þorowgh a strynour þou hom strene;\nTemper hom with almonde mylke anon.\nTake brawne of capons or henne good won,\nTese hit smalle, as I þe lere;\nDo þe ryse in þo mylke over þe fyre,\nLet hit boyle for ony nede;\nCharge hit with tesyd flesshe in dede;\nSeson hit with sugar, and floresshe\nWith fryud almondes þo lordes dysshe.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Þandon for wylde digges, swannus, and piggus.[/b]\nTake, wasshe þo isues of swannes anon,\nAnd skoure þo guttus with salt ichon;\nSethe alle to gedur and hew hit smalle.\nÞe flesshe and eke þo guttus with alle;\nTake galingale and gode gyngere\nAnd canel, and grynd hom al in fere;\nAnd myude bred þou take þerto,\nAnd temper hit up with brothe also;\nColoure hit with brend bred or with blode,\nSeson hit with venegur, a lytelle for gode;\nWelle alle togedur in a posnet;\nIn service forthe þou schalt hit sett.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Nombuls.[/b]\nTake þo hert and þo mydruv and þe kydnere,\nAnd hew hom smalle, as I þe lere;\nPresse oute þe blode, wasshe hom þou schalle,\nSethe hom in water and in gode ale;\nColoure hit with brende bred or with blode;\nFors hit with peper and canel gode,\nSett hit to þo fyre, as I þe telle in tale;\nKele hit with a litelle ale,\nAnd set hit downe to serve in sale.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Anoþer maner for noumbuls.[/b]\nTake þe noumbuls of þe veneson,\nIn water and salt þo wasshe hom sone,\nAnd in twynne waters, þou schalt hom sethe;\nGrynd bred and peper with ale full smethe,\nWith þe secunde brothe þou temper hit mun,\nAnd hew þy noumbuls alle and sum;\nAnd boyle þy sew, do hom þer inne,\nOf þys mater þer, no more ne myn.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Charlet.[/b]\nTake swettest mylke, þat þou may have,\nColour hit with safron, so God þe save;\nTake fresshe porke and sethe hit wele,\nAnd hew hit smalle every dele;\nSwyng eyryn, and do þer to;\nSet hit over þe fyre, þenne\nBoyle hit and sture lest hit brenne;\nWhenne hit welles up, þou schalt hit kele\nWith a litel ale, so have þou cele;\nWhen hit is inoȝe, þou sett hit doune,\nAnd kepe hit lest hit be to broune.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For Charlet icoloured.[/b]\nTake almondes unblanchyd, wasshe hom and grynd;\nTemper hom with rede wyne, þat is so kynd;\nAlye hit up with floure of ryce,\nDo þer to pynys and saunders for spyce,\nFor to coloure hit, loke þou do þis,\nAnd oþer goode spyces þou take, iwys,\nBothe strong and swete þou do þer to;\nSalt hit, boyle hit, sethe hit forthe þo,\nWith annes icomfet, florysshe hit þou schalle;\nMesse hit in dysshes to be served in halle.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Iusselle.[/b]\nTake myud bred, and eyren þou swynge;\nDo hom togeder with out lettyng,\nTake fresshe broth of gode befe,\nColoure hit with safron, þat is me lefe,\nBoyle hit softly, and in þo boylyng,\nDo þer to sage and persely ȝoyng.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Breuet de almonde.[/b]\nTake gode almonde mylke anon,\nAnd loke þou lye hit with amydone,\nOr with flowre þat is bake;\nColoure hit with safron, I undurtake;\nFors hit with powder of þy male\nOf gyngere, canel, and galingale.\nTake pertrykes and chykyns and hom wele sethe;\nHew hom in quarters fayre and smethe;\nDo þat mylke over þo fyre þat tyde,\nAnd boyle and sett hit doune besyde,\nAnd florysshe hit with powdur, as I þe kenne,\nÞou may have more menske emong alle menne.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Blonk desore.[/b]\nTake ryse and wasshe hom in a cup,\nGrynd hom smalle and temper up\nWith almonde mylke, so have þou cele;\nDo hit over þo fyre and boyle hit wele;\nTake braune of capons or hennes alle,\nHew hit þat hit be riȝt smalle;\nAnd grynd hit wele, as myud brede,\nAnd do þer to, as I þe rede;\nSeson hit with sugur grete plente,\nWith fryid almondes florysshe so fre.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Bucnade.[/b]\nTake almonde mylke as I con preche;\nColoure hit with safron as I þe teche;\nFors hit with poudur, þat is gode;\nTake larde of porke, wele soþyn, by þo rode;\nHew hit in gobettes wele afyne;\nLoke þey ben smale and put hem inne;\nLye hit with floure or amydone,\nBoyle hit wele and sett hit done;\nFlorysshe hit with powdur, as I þe kenne,\nÞenne may hit be served, before gode men.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Rose.[/b]\nTake flour of ryse, as whyte as sylke,\nAnd hit welle, with almond mylke;\nBoyle hit tyl hit be chargyd, þenne\nTake braune of capone or elle of henne;\nLoke þou grynd hit wondur smalle,\nAnd sithen þou charge hit with alle;\nColoure with alkenet, sawnder, or ellys with blode,\nFors hit with clowes or macys gode;\nSeson hit with sugur grete plenté,\nÞis is a rose, as kokes telle me.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Lede lardes.[/b]\nTake eyren and swete mylke of a cow,\nSwyng hom togedur, as I byd now;\nTake larde of fresshe porke with alle,\nSethe hit and schere hit on peses smalle;\nCast þer in and boyle hit, þenne\nStyr hit wele, as I þe kenne,\nTyl hit be gedered on crud harde;\nLeche hit, and rost hit afterwarde\nApone a gredel, þen serve þou may\nHit forthe, with spit, as I þe say.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For blanchyd mortrews.[/b]\nSethe hennes and porke, þat is fulle fresshe;\nBray almondes unblanchyd and temper hom nesshe\nWith clene brothe, and drawe hom þo;\nAlay þy flesshe smalle grounden to,\nAnd floure of ryce þou grynd also;\nCast powder of gyngere and sugur þerinne,\nBut loke þat hit be not to þyn,\nBut stondand and saltid mesurlé\nAnd kepe þy dysshe mete for þo maystré.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Peions istued.[/b]\nTake peions and hew hom in morselle smalle,\nPut hom in a erþyn pot, þou shalle;\nTake pilled garlek and herbys anon,\nHack hom smalle er þou more don;\nPut hom in þo pot, and þer to take\nGode brothe with wyte grece, þou noȝt forsake;\nDo powdur þer to and gode verius,\nColoure hit with safron, and salt inow;\nÞou put in pote þese þynges alle,\nAnd stue þy peions þus þou schalle.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Sowpus dorre.[/b]\nTake almondes, bray hem, wryng hom up;\nBoyle hom with wyn rede to sup;\nÞen temper hom with wyn, salt, I rede,\nAnd loke þou tost fyne wete brede,\nAnd lay in dysshes, dubene with wyne;\nDo in þis dysshes mete, þat is so fyne;\nMesse hit forthe, and florysshe hit þenne\nWith sugur and gynger, as I þe kenne.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Gruel of almondes.[/b]\nTake almondes unblanchid and bray hom sone,\nPut ote mele to, þenne hase þou done,\nAnd grynde alle sammen, and draw hit þenne\nWith water and sethe, as I þe kenne;\nColoure hit with safron and salt hit þenne,\nAnd set in sale byfore gode menne.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Ioutus de almonde.[/b]\nTake erbe, perboyle hom, fayre and wele;\nHew hom and grynde hom every dele;\nTake almondes unblanched and grynd hom smalle,\nDrawȝe hom with water, I wote þou schalle;\nSet hit over þe fyre, þyn erbis þou sethe\nWith þo mylke forsayde, þat grounden is smethe;\nCast þerto sugur, and salt anone;\nTake þer þy ioutes made dalmone.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Caudel dalmone.[/b]\nTake almondes unblanchyd and hom þou bray;\nDrawe hom up with wyn, I dar wele say;\nÞer to do pouder of good gyngere\nAnd sugur, and boyle alle þese in fere,\nAnd coloure hit with safron and salt hit wele,\nAnd serve hit forthe Sir at þo mele.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Buttur of Almonde mylke.[/b]\nTake thykke mylke of almondes clere,\nBoyle wele alle in fere;\nAnd in þo boylyng, cast þerinne\nVenegur, oþer ellys gode wyne;\nDo hit soþenne in a canvas þenne,\nIn soþun, gar hit on hepe to renne;\nIn clothe þou henge hit a myle way,\nAnd after in colde water þou hit lay;\nServe hit forthe in þe dysshe,\nÞat day þo lorde is servyd with fysshe.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Ryse.[/b]\nTake ryse and wasshe and grynde hem smalle,\nTemper hom with almonde mylke þou schalle;\nDrauȝe hom thorowghe a streynour clene,\nBoyle hom and seson hom with sugur schene;\nFors hit with fryude almondes gode,\nÞen hase þou done, syr, by þo rode.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Kaudel Ferry.[/b]\nTake almondes unblanchyd, so have þou cele,\nAnd wasshe hom fayre and grynd hom wele;\nTemper hom up with wyne so clene,\nAnd drauȝe hom þorowgh a canvas shene;\nIn pot þou coloure hit with safron,\nAnd lye hit up with Amydone,\nOr with floure of ryse so fre;\nRyȝt thykke loke þou þat be;\nSeson hit with sugur grete plenté,\nFlorysshe hit with maces, I tel þe.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For to make a rape.[/b]\nTake raysyns of corauns þerto,\nAnd wyte wynne þou take also;\nSethe þenne oþer raysyns grete\nIn rede wyne, and boyle a lytul with hete;\nDo opon a broche, rost hom bydene\nA lytel, and take hom fayre and clene\nAnd bray hom in a morter smalle,\nA crust of brede þou bray with alle.\nPut alle in þe pot with grythe,\nÞo raysyns of corauns, þo swete wyne with,\nA lytul vengur, and pouder take þo\nOf clowes, maces and quibibis to;\nBoyle alle to geder, and serve hit þenne,\nAnd sett hit forthe before goode men.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Mylke rostyd.[/b]\nTake swete mylke and put in panne,\nSwyng eyren with alle, grynde safron\nAnd do þerto; welle hit þenne,\nTylle hit wax thykke, as I þe kenne;\nAnd sethe and sye hit thorowghe a cloth,\nPresse hit, þat leves, withouten othe;\nWhen hit is colde, leche hit with knyves;\nRost hit, and messe hit forthe on schyves.
