(English, XV c.)\n[b]For to make a potage of welkes.[/b]\nTake welkes and wasshe fayre, in blythe,\nIn water, and take whyte salt þerwith\nAnd after hakke hom on a borde,\nAs smalle as þou may, at a worde,\nAnd bray hom in a morter clere;\nSethe hom in mylke over þe fyre;\nOf almondes or of a clow þou take schalle,\nLye hit with amydone þerwith alle;\nColoure hit with safrone, and do þerinne\nPoudur of peper, or goode comyne.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For to make potage of oysturs.[/b]\nPerboyle þyn oysturs and take hom oute;\nKepe welle þy bre with outen doute,\nAnd hakke hom on a borde full smalle,\nAnd bray in a morter þou schalle;\nDo hom in hor owne brothe for goode,\nDo mylke of almondes þer to by þe rode,\nAnd lye hit up with amydone,
(English, XV c.)\n[b]And frye smalle mynsud onyone[/b]\nIn oyle, or sethe hom in mylke þou schalle;\nDo powdur þerto of spyces withalle,\nAnd coloure hit þenne with safron gode;\nHit is holden restoratyf fode.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Sauge Seynes.[/b]\nTake swynes fete and sethe hom clene,\nTake ȝolkes of eyren þat harde bene,\nAnd sage as mykul as fall þerto,\nGode powdur, and temper with venegur;\nWhen þou hase soþyn þo fete ryȝt welle,\nClovyn hom and paryd hom þer tylle,\nLay hom on dysshe with blythe,\nÞo sawce on þe ȝolkes þerwyth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For to make a compost.[/b]\nTake þo chekyns and hew hom for þo seke,\nAll but þe hede and þe legges eke;\nTake a handfulle of herb lovache,\nAnd anoþer of persely, als\nOf sage þat never was founde fals,\nAnd noþer of lekes and alle hom wasshe\nÞose herbes in water, þat rennes so rasshe;\nBreke þorowghe þy honde, bothe herbe and leke,\nWith a pynt of hony enbeny hom eke,\nSumme of þese herbes þou shalle laye\nIn þe pottus bothun, as I þe say;\nSumme of þe chekyns þou put þerto,\nAnd þen of þe herbȝ do to also;\nSo of þo ton so of þat oþer,\nÞo herbȝ on þe last my dere brother;\nAbove þese herbus a lytul larde\nSmalle myncyd, haldand togeder warde;\nTake powder of gynger and canel god wone,\nCast on þese oþer thynges everychon;\nBe sleȝe and powre in water þenne\nTo myd þo pot, as I the kenne;\nOpone þo bruys poure hit withinne,\nAnd cover hit þat no hete oute wynne,\nAnd tendurly seyth hit þou do may,\nSalt hit, serve hit, as I þe say.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Blanc maungere of fysshe.[/b]\nTake a pownde of ryse and sethe hom wele,\nTyl þat þay brostene; and lete hom kele.\nMylke of almondes þerto þou cast,\nÞo tenche or lampray do to on last;\nWelle alle togeder, as I þe kenne,\nAnd messe hit forthe before godde men.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Mortrews of fysshe.[/b]\nTake þo kelkes of fysshe anon,\nAnd þo lyver of þo fysshe, sethe hom alon;\nÞen take brede and peper and ale,\nAnd temper þo brothe fulle welle þou schalle,\nAnd welle hit togeder and serve hit þenne,\nAnd set in sale before good mene.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For to make rose dalmoyne.[/b]\nTake whyte pese and wasshe hom wele,\nTylle þat þey hulle, sethe yche adele,\nAnd bene clene of þam, þen schalle þou caste\nIn to þo pot and cover in hast;\nAnd loke no brethe þer passe oute,\nBut boyle hom wele with owtyn dowte;\nOf almonde mylke þou kest þerto,\nOf floure of ryse and salt also;\nColoure hit with safrone and messe hit, þenne\nSet hit in sale before goode men.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For a kolys.[/b]\nÞe brawne take of sothun henne or chekyne,\nAnd hew hit smalle and bray þen with wyne,\nWith ote grotis, and whyte brede eke;\nWith þe brothe of henne þou tempur hit meke;\nTake oute þe bonys and grynd hit smalle,\nIn to þe brothe þou kast hit alle,\nAnd sye hit thurgh a clothe clene;\nDose hit, and serve hit forthe bydene.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Gruel of Porke.[/b]\nTake brawne of swyne, perboyle hit wele,\nAnd grynde hit smalle, Syr, everydele;\nWith ȝolkes of eyren þou schalle hit lye,\nSet hit over þe fyre for-þye,\nPut whyte grece þerto, bewar, iwys,\nLet hit not sethe lest þou mys.\nDo þer to powder and safron þenne\nAnd messe hit forthe before goode menne;\nPowder dowce þeron þou kast\nStondande at dressore on þe last.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Conyngus in cyne.[/b]\nSmyte þe conyngus in pese smalle;\nAnd sethe hom in brothe gode þou shalle;\nMynsyn onyons in grece þou sethe,\nAnd in good brothe, þat is so smethe\nWalle togeder; and drauȝe alioure\nOf blode and brede sumdele sowre,\nSesonut with venegur and good brothe eke,\nKast salt þerto and powder fulle meke.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Harus in cyne.[/b]\nPerboyle þe hare and larde hit wele,\nSethyn loke þou rost hir everydele;\nTake onyons and loke þou hew hom smalle,\nFrye hom in grece, take peper and ale,\nAnd grynde togeder þo onyons also;\nColoure hit with safrone and welle hit þo;\nLay þe hare in charioure, as I þe kenne;\nPowre on þe sewe and serve hit þenne.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Harus in a sewe.[/b]\nAlle rawe þo hare schalle hacked be,\nIn gobettis smalle, Syr, levys me;\nIn hir owne blode seyn or sylud clene,\nGrynde brede and peper withalle bydene;\nÞenne temper hit with þe same bre,\nÞenne boyled and salted hit servyd schalle be.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Harus in abrotet.[/b]\nHew smalle þy hare in gobetus gode,\nSethe hom in brothe with alle his blode;\nWhen hit is soþun wondur wele,\nDrawȝh thurgh a streynour, so have þou cele;\nTake almondes unblanchid, wasshe hom and grynde;\nWith self brothe temper hom by kynde;\nTake onyons and perboyle hom þou mot,\nAnd dresshe hom smalle, kest hom in pot\nWith alle oþer thyngus, and cast þer to\nWith venegur and salt, þen hase þou doo.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Harus in Perdoylyse.[/b]\nTake harys and perboyle hom, I rede,\nIn goode brothe, kele hit for drede,\nAnd hew þy flesshe and cast þerinne.\nTake swongen eggus, no more ne myn,\nAnd cast in þy sewe and sethe hit þenne.\nTake obles and wafrons, as I þe kenne,\nClose hom in dysshes fare and wele;\nSalt þe sewe, so have þou cele,\nAnd lay hit above as gode men done,\nAnd messe hit forthe, Syr, at þo none.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Hennes in brewes.[/b]\nWith porke þou sethe þo henne fatte,\nGrynde brede and peper and be not batte;\nAnd comyne also þou schalle grynde,\nSeson hom with ale, þat is hor kynde;\nWith þo brothe of hennes þou temper hit shalle,\nBoyle hit, coloure hit, salt hit withalle;\nServe hom forthe, as þou may see,\nÞese er hennes in browet, levys þou me.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Chekyns in browet.[/b]\nTake chekyns, scalde hom fayre and clene;\nTake persole, sauge, oþer herbȝ, grene\nGrapus, and stope þy chekyns with wynne;\nTake goode brothe, sethe hom þerinne,\nSo þat þay sone boyled may be;\nColoure þe brothe with safrone fre,\nAnd cast þeron powder dowce,\nFor to be served in goode mennys howse.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Chekyns in Cawdel.[/b]\nIn brothe þou boyle þy chekyns gode;\nTake ȝolkes of eyren, Syr, for þo rode,\nAlye hom up with brothe forsayde;\nTake powder gynger, abrayde,\nAnd sugur, and rew, and safron clere,\nAnd salt, and set hit over þo fyre;\nWith owtyn boylyng messe hit forthe þenne;\nÞy chekyns hole take, I þe kenne,\nOf þay be brokyn, on dysshe hom lay,\nHelde hom þe sewe, as I þe say.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For to boyle fesawantes and pertryks.[/b]\nTake goode brothe, þerin þou pyt\nÞy fesauntes and þy pertryks, þat men may wyt.\nDo þerto ale, floure, peper fre,\nOf hole canel, good quantité;\nAnd let alle sethe þerwyth fulle wele,\nAnd messe hit forthe, Syr, at þe mele.\nPowder dowce þerin þou cast,\nWhen hit is servyd on þe last.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Roo in a Sewe.[/b]\nTake þo roo, pyke hit clene forthy;\nBoyle hit þou shalt and after hit drye;\nHew hit on gobettis, þat ben smalle,\nDo hit in pot withalle;\nKest wyn þerto, if þou do ryȝt,\nTake persole and sawge and ysope bryȝt,\nWasshe hom and hew hom wondur smalle,\nAnd do þerto hit þou schalle,\nColoure hit with blode or sawnders hors.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Hennes in gravé.[/b]\nTake hennes and rost, as I þe kenne,\nSithinn, hew hom smalle and frye hom; þenne\nTake wyne or peper or venegur to,\nGrynd hit togeder with hennes þo;\nLye hit with ȝolkes of eyren wele,\nColoure hit with safrone everydele,\nAnd messe hit forthe withoutene ony more,\nAnd loke þou forȝete noȝt þys lore.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Capons in Covisye.[/b]\nTake capons and sethe hom wele,\nAnd hew hom smalle ilkadele;\nTake peper and brede, and grynde hit smalle,\nAnd temper hit up with capon alle;\nTake whyȝte of eyren harde soþun þo,\nAnd hake hom smalle and do þerto,\nAnd boyle þe capon and coloure hit þenne\nWith safrone, and do as I kenne;\nÞo ȝolkes of eggus, I telle þe,\nAlle hole þou put in disshe so fre.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Hennes in gauncel.[/b]\nTake first and rost welle þy henne,\nTake garlek by hit selfe and grynd; þenne\nBlonde hit with mylke and put alle in panne,\nAnd hew þyn henne and do þer to þenne\nÞy henne and ȝolkes of eyren imelle;\nColoure hit with safron and let hit welle,\nAnd messe hit forthe, I telle þe;
(English, XV c.)\n[b]But þou wille alye hit with floure so fre.[/b]\nLamprayes in browet.\n\nTake lamprayes and scalde hom by kynde,\nSythyn, rost hom on gredyl, and grynde\nPeper and safrone; welle hit with alle,\nDo þo lampreyes and serve hit in sale.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Lamprayes in galentine.[/b]\nTake lamprayes and hom let blode\nAt þo navel, and scalde hom for gode;\nRost hom þenne, and þou hom laye\nAlle hole in platere, as I þe saye;\nServe with galentine, made in sale,\nWith gyngere, canel and galingale.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For tenchis in gravé.[/b]\nSethe þy tenchis, and after hom brede,\nAnd rost hom on a gredel, I rede;\nGrynd peper and safron with ale, I kenne,\nWith tenchis brothe, þou temper hit; þenne\nLay þo tenche opon a platere fayre,\nDo on þat browet withouten disware.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Chawdewyne de boyce.[/b]\nTake smalle notes, schale not kurnele,\nAs þou dose of almondes, fayre and wele;\nFrye hom in oyle, þen sethe hom ryȝt\nIn almonde mylke þat is bryȝt;\nÞen þou schalle do in floure of ryce\nAnd also oþer pouder of spyce;\nFry oþer curneles besyde also,\nColoure þou hit with safron, or þou fer goo,\nTo divers þo mete þou schalt hit set,
(English, XV c.)\n[b]With þo fryed curnels with outen let.[/b]\nCapons in Cassolyce.\n\nTake capons and schalde and pyke hom þen;\nÞe skyn þou opon, as I þe kenne,\nBe hynde þo hede, blaw hym with penne;\nÞenne ryses þo skyn before,\nRayse up þo skyn alle hole abowte,\nTake porke and hen flesshe with outen doute,\nAnd ȝolkes of eyren and gode powder;\nOf alle þo thynges þou make farsure,\nAnd farse þo skyn and perboyle hit wele;\nÞen larde þo capone, rost hym yche dele;\nOf almonde mylke and amydone\nMake bater, and coloure hit anone\nWith safron; serve hit at fyre rostande,\nEnbene hit wele withe þy ryȝt honde.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For to make momene.[/b]\nTake whyte wyne, I telle þe,\nAnd sugur þerto ryȝt grete plenté;\nTake, bray þo brawne of aȝt capon;\nTo a pot of oyle of on galon,\nAnd of hony a qwharte þou take;\nDo hit þer to as ever þou wake,\nTake powder þo mountenaunce of a pownde,\nAnd galingale ginger and canel rownde,\nAnd cast þer to, and styre hit; þenne\nAlle in on pot sethe hit, I kenne.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Lange de beof.[/b]\nTake þo ox tonge and schalle hit wele,\nSethe hit, broche hit in larde yche dele,\nWith cloves of gelofer hit broch þou shalle,\nÞen do hit to fyre and rost hit alle;\nWith ȝolkes of eyren enbene hit ay\nWhille þat hit rostes, as I þe say.\nÞen take blode, þat is so lefe,\nWelle hit in fresshe brothe of þe befe,\nBray hit fulle wele in on mortere,\nDo in fayre grece, þat is so clere;\nFors hit with spicys ryȝt gode with alle,\nAnd sythun, serve hit in to þe halle;\nTo þe forsayde tonge þis sawce is dyȝt,\nHere endes oure potage fulle gode ryȝt.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Pro Salsamentis. -- To make sawce.[/b]\nNow speke I wylle of sauces sere:\nHow þay ar made, I wylle ȝow lere,\nNext after potage þay servyd schalle be,\nAs I have lurned in þys cuntré.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Pur verde sawce.[/b]\nTake persole, peletre an oyns, and grynde,\nTake whyte bred myude by kynde,\nTemper alle up with venegur or wyne,\nForce hit with powder of peper fyne.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Sawce for Mawdelardes rosted.[/b]\nTake onyons and hew hom wele,\nPut sum in þo mawdelarde, so have þou cele,\nAnd hacke mo onyons, as I þe kenne;\nWith þo grece of þo mawdelarde þou sethe hom, þen\nTake ale, mustarde and hony þo,\nBoyle alle togeder or þou more do;\nFor maularde rosted þys sawce is dyȝt,\nAnd served in sale by gode ryȝt.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Sawce for vele and venysone.[/b]\nTake brede and frye hit in grece þou schalle,\nWith brothe of venegur drawȝe hit withalle,\nKast powder of gynger anon þer to\nAnd peper, and sethe þo\nAnd messe hit forthe; a sawce hit is\nFor vele and venyson, iwys.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Blaunche sawce for capons.[/b]\nTake blanchid almondis and smal hom grynde,\nTemper hom with verius, þat is hor kynde,\nPowder of gynger, and kast þer to,\nAnd messe hit forthe, þen hase þou do.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Sawce best for capons rostyd.[/b]\nTake lyver of capons and rost hom wele,\nTake annes and grynd hit, as have þou cele,\nPare gynger and canel gode þer to,\nA lytel crust of brede þou take also;\nGrynde al þese þynges wondur smalle,\nWith verius temper hom up þou schalle;\nWith grece of capons boyle hit in syȝt\nAnd serve hit forthe fulle wele þou myȝt.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Sawce sirer for mawdelardus.[/b]\nTake brede and blode iboylyd and grynde,\nAnd drawȝhe hit þorowghe a clothe by kynde,\nWith venegur gode and sesounabulle,\nWith powder of gynger, and peper abulle,\nAnd grece of mawdelarde; and boyle alle wele,\nAnd messe hit forthe Syr at þo mele.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Gawncel for þe gose.[/b]\nTake garlek and grynde hit wele forþy,\nTemper hit with water a lytel, perdy;\nPut floure þer to and also salt,\nColour hit with safron I wot þou schalt;\nTemper hit up with cow-mylke þo,\nAnd sethe hit and serve hit forthe also.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Sawce for swannus.[/b]\nTake þo offal and þo lyver of þo swan,\nIn gode brothe þou sethe hom þan;\nWhen hit is sothyne, take oute þe bonus,\nSmalle hew þo flesshe, Syr, for þe nonus;\nMake alyoure of crust of brede,\nOf blode of swanne, þat soþun is lede,\nCaste powdur of gynger and clawes þer to,\nOf peper and wyn þou take also,\nAnd salt hit þen and sethe hit wele;\nCast in þy flesshe, hewen yche a dele,\nAnd messe hit forthe, as I þe kenne,\nSet hit in sale before goode menne.
(English, XV c.)\n[b][Sawce] For cranys and herons.[/b]\nThe crane is enarmed ful wele I wot\nWith larde of porke at on bare mot,\nRostyd and eten with gode gingere,\nÞat is þo sawce þat servis þere;\nÞo heroun is rosted, as have I blys,\nAnd eton with gynger as his kynde is.
(English, XV c.)\n[b][Sawce] For pekokys and pertrikis.[/b]\nPekokys and pertrikys perboylyd schyn be,\nLardyd, rostyd, eton, levys me,\nWith gyngere, payndmayn paryd clene\nAnd groundyn in a morter, þat is schene,\nTemperid up with venegur gode,\nWith powder of gyngere and salt, by þo rode,\nAnd drawȝen þorowghe a streynour mylde,\nServid forthe with pekok and pertrik wylde.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Galentyne.[/b]\nTake crust of brede and grynde hit smalle,\nTake powder of galingale and temper with alle\nPowder of gyngere and salt also;\nTemper hit with venegur er þou more do,\nDrawȝe hit þurughe a streynour þenne,\nAnd messe hit forthe before gode menne.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Sawce camelyne, kervelettes and oþer thyngus.[/b]\nTake raysons of corouns and kyrnels smalle\nOf notes, and do away þo schale,\nTake crust of brede and clowe in fere,\nAnd powder imaked of gode gyngere,\nFlowre of canel þou schalle take, þenne\nBray alle togedur, as I þe kenne,\nIn a morter and salt þerto;\nTemper alle with venegur, þen hase þou do,\nAnd messe hit forthe; þis is sawce fyne,\nÞat men calles camelyne.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For lumbardus mustard.[/b]\nTake mustarde and let hit drye\nAnonyn, Sir, wyturlye;\nStomper hit in a morter fyne,\nAnd fars hit þurghe a clothe of lyne;\nDo wyne þerto and venegur gode,\nSture hom wele togeder for þe rode,\nAnd make hit þyke inowghe þenne,\nWhenne þou hit spendes byfore gode menne,\nAnd make hit thynne with wyne, I say,\nWith diverse metes þou serve hit may.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For Pykulle.[/b]\nTake droppyng of capone rostyd wele\nWith wyne and mustarde, as have þou cele,\nWith onyons smalle schrad and sothun in grece,\nMeng alle in fere and forthe hit messe.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Filetus in Galentine.[/b]\nTake filetes of porke and half hom rost,\nSmyte hom in peses with outene bost;\nDrawȝe a lyoure of blode and brede withalle,\nDo venegur þer to, I wot þou schalle;\nFors hit with powder of canel, or gode gynger,\nSethe hit with þo flesshe, alle in fere;\nSalt and messe forthe, þenne\nSet hit in sale before gode menne.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Pigges in sawce.[/b]\nTake pigges and scalde hom in water clene,\nSethe hom in water and salt bydene;\nTake hom up and lete hom kele;\nTake persoley and sage, and grynde hit wele\nWith þe brothe of pigges with owtene rewarde,\nAnd ȝolkes of eggus þat soþun ar harde,\nTemper alle with venegur sumdele stondande;\nLay pigges in a vessayle, with bothe hande,\nHeld þy sawce a-bofe tolde forþy,\nAnd serve hit alle forthe, Syr, wyturly.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Sawce madame.[/b]\nTake sawge, persoly, ysope, saveray,\nOnyons gode, peres, garlek, I say,\nAnd grapes; go fille þy gose þenne\nAnd sew þy hole, no grece oute renne;\nLay hur to fyre and rost hyr browne,\nAnd kepe þo grece þat falles doune.\nTake galingale and þo grece þat renne,\nDo hit in posnet, as I þe kenne;\nWhenne þo gose is rostyd, take hir away,\nSmyte hir in pesys, I þe pray;\nÞat is within, þou schalle take oute,\nKest in þy posnet with outene doute;\nȝif hit is thyke do þerto wyne,\nAnd powder of galingale þat is fyne,\nAnd powder dowce and salt also;\nBoyle alle togeder er þou fyr go,\nIn a dysshe þy gose þou close\nÞe sawce abofe, as I suppose.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Gose in a Hogge pot.[/b]\nIn pesis þou schalle þy gose stryke,\nTake water and wyne bothe ilyke;\nDo in þy gose; and onyons þou take\nA gode quantité, as I er spake,\nAnd erbus hacked þou take also,\nAnd cast þou in er þou more do;\nþen set þy pot over þo fyre,\nAnd hit wele stir for þe hyre;\nAnd make a lyoure of brede and blode,\nAnd lye hit þerwithe, for hit is gode;\nKast powder þerto and salt anon,
(English, XV c.)\n[b]And messe hit, þenne þou hase done.[/b]\nTo save venysone fresshe over þe ȝer.\n\nYf þou wylle kepe þe tayle of a dere\nFresshe in seson over þo ȝere,\nOr oþer venesone yf þat hit nede,\nÞus schalt þu do, I wot in dede;\nPresse out þo blode, for anythyng\nÞat is cause for grete rotyng;\nIn erþyne pot þou shalt hit pyt\nAnd feyre hony do into hit;\nTo þo hony stonde over þo flesshe\nToo fyngurs thyke for harde or nesshe;\nWith leder þo mouthe þen schalt þou bynde,\nKepe hit fro ayre, son or wynde,\nIn cofer, or huche or seler merke.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For to save venysone fro restyng.[/b]\nTake venesone when hit is new slayn,\nAnd cover hit alle with ferne playn\nÞat no wynde enter þer to;\nAnd whenne þou hast covered hit so,\nLede hit home, selor hit lay\nÞat wynde ne sone ne ughe hit may;\nDresse hit wele and wassh hit clene,\nSythen, lay hit in water alle by dene,\nÞer in be half a day to lye;\nÞenne take hit oute on flore to drye,\nÞenne after take salt a quantité;\nBoyle hit in clene water so fre,\nAnd kele hit, þat he be bot lue,\nAnd þerin wasshe þy venesone true,\nAnd let hit lye þerin thre dayes\nAnd thre nyȝhtes, by any kyns wayes;\nThen take hit oute of þat water,\nSalt hit wyth drye salt, alle in fere.\nAnd do hit in a barel þenne;\nÞe barel staf ful as I þe kenne,\nStop wele þo hede for wynde and sone,\nFor hit wylle payre þo venysone.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To keep herbȝ over þe wyntur.[/b]\nTake floure and rere þo cofyns fyne,\nWele stondande withouten stine;\nTake tenderons of sauge with owte lesyng,\nAnd stop one fulle up to þo ryng;\nÞenne close þo lyd fayre and wele,\nÞat ayre go not oute never a dele,\nDo so with saveray, percil and rewe;\nAnd þenne bake hom harde, wel neȝe brende;\nSythun, kepe hom drye and to hom tent;\nÞis powder schalle be of more vertu,\nÞen opone erþe when hit gru.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For lyoure best.[/b]\nTake drye floure, in cofyne hit close,\nAnd bake hit hard, as I suppose;\nÞou may hit kepe alle þys fyve ȝere,\nÞere-with alye mony metes sere;\nHere endys oure sawce, þat I foretolde.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]De cibis assatis.[/b]\nOf rostyd mete now speke I wolde,\nFor þer bene bestes þat schyne be rost,\nAs conyng, pigges, ful wele þou wost,\nAnd foules also þat rostyd schyne be\nOn diverse manere in her degré;\nAnd kostyf of motone, þat I wele knaw,\nEnbrochyd shal be, by ryȝt gode law;\nAnd also fysshe þou schalle enbroche,\nAs porpays þat swymmes by þo see roche;\nÞerfore I telle ȝou now, I rede,\nWhat schalle rost with neck and hede.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For þe crane.[/b]\nÞo crane schalle fyrst enarmed be,\nScalde and pulde ful warlé,\nDraȝun at þo syde as wodcockis,\nWith legges al hole he rostyd is;\nAbowte þo brothe þo necke þou cralle,\nPut in þo bylle at coler þou schalle;\nEnarme hym forthe as hit is tolde\nBefore, and serve þys crane bolde.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For heroun rostyd.[/b]\nÞe heroun is slayn, as have I sene;\nÞe herte oute pyke alle bydene,\nUnder þe lyft wyng þo neck bone steke,\nDevoyded, as men me tolde meke;\nÞenne under þo wynge þo skyn þou cralle,\nPyt in þo bylle at coler þou schalle.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For wodcock, snyȝt and curlue.[/b]\nTo wodcok, snype, curlue also,\nÞe betore in fere with hom schalle goo;\nAlle schun be draȝun, Syr, at þo syde,\nAnd honestly rostyd with outene pryde,\nWith neck and hede suande in fere,\nÞo bylle put þurghe þo þeȝes sere;\nOn alle þese fowles þo legges schune bene,\nSumme cralled, sum streȝt, as I have sene.\nAnd gret as heroun rostyd schalle be,\nÞat a knyȝt is called for gentloré,\nA capone also þat comyn is,\nÞo pecok wyth his tayle so have I blys,\nÞo fesaunt kok, but not þo henne;\nÞus have I lurnet at gentil men;\nAlle oþer foles þat swymmen in flode,\nÞat schun be rostyd, Syr, by þo rode,\nWith outen necke or hede, I trowe,\nAnd oþer smalle bryddes, þat I wele knaw,\nAs osel, smityng, laveroc gray,\nPertryk, werkock, I dayr wele say;\nÞo kormorount schalle rost iwys,\nWith þo bylle opone for grete koyntes.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For pygges farsyd.[/b]\nTake swongen eyrene and floure þer to,\nAnd powder of peper er þou more do;\nBlend alle togeder and salt þerwith;\nColoure hit with safrone, so have þou blythe;\nPut alle in body of þo pygge,\nRost hit on broche of irne bygge\nEnfarsed; þo cle of pygge schalle be\nFestened in þe cheke so mot þou þe;\nÞo hender legges enoynt þou schalle,\nÞo cles by þo sydes þou festun withalle.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For fraunche mele.[/b]\nTake swongene eyrene in bassyne clene,\nAnd kreme of mylke þat is so schene,\nAnd myyd bred, þou put þer to,\nAnd powder of peper er þou more do;\nColoure hit with safrone in hast,\nAnd kremelyd sewet of schepe on last,\nAnd fylle þy bagge þat is so gode,\nAnd sew hit fast, Syr, for þo rode;\nWhenne hit is soþun, þou schalt hit leche,\nAnd broyle hyt on gredel, as I þe teche.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For bours.[/b]\nTake porke and gese, hew hom þou schalle\nOn gobetes, with powder of peper withalle;\nHom sethe in pot þat is so clene,\nWith oute any water, with salt, I wene;\nFro Martyn messe to gode tyde evyne,\nÞys mete wylle serve, þou may me lene,\nAt dyner or soper, if þat hit nede;\nÞou take gode ale, þat is not quede,\nÞer in þou boyle þo forsayde mete\nÞo more worship þou may gete.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For powme dorrys.[/b]\nTake porke and grynde hit rawe, I kenne,\nTemper hit with swongen egges; þenne\nKast powder to make hit on a balle;\nIn playand water þou kast hit schalle\nTo harden, þenne up þou take,\nEnbroche hit fayre for goddes sake.\nEndore hit with ȝolkes of egges þen\nWith a fedyr at fyre, as I þe kenne;\nBothe grene and rede þow may hit make\nWith iuse of herbȝ I undertake;\nHalde under a dysshe þat noȝt be lost,\nMore honest hit is as þou wele wost.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Hasteletes on fysshe day.[/b]\nTake fyggus quartle, and raysyns, þo\nHole dates, almondes, rine hom also\nOn broche of irne, and rost hom sone;\nEndore hom with ȝolkes of egges anone.\nHere endys oure hastere þat I of spake;\nTo speke of bakun mete I wolde clake,\nFor lamprays, darials and flaunes also,\nAnd oþer metes mony and moo.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For lamprays bakun.[/b]\nFyrst scalde þy lamprays fayre and wele,\nAs I tolde byfore, so have þou cele;\nSoþun, rere a cofyne of flowre so fre,\nRolle in þo lampray, as hit may be;\nTake mynsud onyons þer to, gode wonne,\nBut fyrst take powder of peper, anon\nOf maces, cloves and graynys also,\nAnd dates al hole þou take þerto,\nPoure rede wyne þerto þou schalle,\nColoure hit with safrone and closen alle.\nIn myddes þo lydde an tuel þou make,\nSet hit in þo ovyn for to bake;\nȝete take hit oute, fede hit with wyne,\nLay on þo tuel a past fulle fyne,\nAnd bake hit forthe, as I þe kenne,\nTo serve in sale before gode menne.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For darials.[/b]\nTake creme of almonde mylke iwys,\nAnd ȝolkes of eyren, so have þou blys,\nAnd make a batere þat is ful gode,\nAnd rere a cofyne with mylde mode;\nAnd sethe a mawdelarde, þat fat is þenne,\nAnd cut in peses, as I þe kenne;\nSquare as dises þou shalt hit make,\nKast hit in batere, and powder þou take\nOf gynger, of kanel, þat gode is, þo\nEnfors hit wele er þou more do,\nAnd loke þy cofyne be hardened wele,\nPowre in þy batere, so have þou cele,\nWith a disshe hit florysshe þou may,\nWith blanchyd almondes, as I þe say.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For flaunes.[/b]\nTake new chese and grynde hit fayre,\nIn morter with egges, with out dysware;\nPut powder þer to of sugur, I say,\nColoure hit with safrone ful wele þou may;\nPut hit in cofyns þat bene fayre,\nAnd bake hit forthe, I þe pray.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For custanes.[/b]\nGrynde porke, brek eyren þer to anon,\nWith powder of peper er þou more done;\nPut hit in cofyn, þat harde is bake,\nAnd ȝolke of egge þen shalt þou take,\nThat harde is soþun, lay in to þo top\nAs hit were a gyldene knop.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For risshens.[/b]\nTake grounden porke þat soþun hase bene\nWith peper and swongen egges clene;\nPut berme þer to, I undertake,\nAs tome as belle hit wille hit make;\nLay hit in a roller as sparlyng fysshe,\nFrye hit in grece, lay hit in dysshe.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For freture.[/b]\nWith egges and floure in batere þou make,\nPut berme þer to, I undertake;\nColoure hit with safrone er þou more do;\nTake powder of peper and cast þer to,\nKerve appuls overtwert and cast þerin,\nFrye hom in grece, no more ne mynne.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Crustate of flesshe.[/b]\nTake peiuns and smalle chekuns with alle\nAnd oþer smale bryddes, and hew hom smalle;\nAnd sethe hom alle togedur þoo\nIn brothe and in white grece, also\nIn verius, and do þer to safroune;\nFyrst make a fole trap þou mun,\nPynche hym, cowche hym þy flesshe þerby;\nKast þerin raysyns of corouns forthy,\nAnd powder dowce and salt gode won;\nBreke eyren and streyne hom thorowghe a clothe anone,\nAnd swyng þy sewe þerwyth þenne,\nAnd helde hit onne þe flesshe I kenne,\nAnd kover þy trap and hele hit wele,\nAnd serve hit forthe, Syr, at þe mele.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Loysyns.[/b]\nIn erthen pot put brothe for hast;\nTake floure of payndemayn, and make þy past\nWith water, þer of þy fele þou make\nWith a roller, and drye hit, I undurtake\nAȝayne þo sonne þat hit be harde;\nKast þerin brothe and make rewarde;\nTo sethe hom take rawe chese anone\nAnd grate hit in disshes mony on\nWith powder dowce; and lay þer in\nÞy loseyns abofe þe chese with wynne,\nAnd powder on last spryngil hit þou may;
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Þose loysyns er harde to make in fay.[/b]\nTartlotes.\n\nTake porke sothun, and grynde hit wele\nWith safroune, and medel hit ylkadel\nWith egges and raysyns of corouns; þo\nTake powder and salt, and do þerto;\nMake a fole of doghe, and close þis fast,\nThis flesshe þat hewene was open þo last\nKover hit with lyddes, and pynche hit fayre,\nKorven in þe myddes two loyseyns a payr,\nSet hit with fryed almondes sere,\nAnd coloure þe past with safroune dere,\nAnd bake hit forthe, as I þe kenne,\nAnd set in sale before gode menne.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Chewetes on fysshe day.[/b]\nTake turbut, haddok, and gode codlyng,\nHacke hit, sethe hit, with owte lesyng,\nAnd grynde hit smale, do dates þerto\nIgroundene, and raysyns and prunus also,\nWith gode powder and salt on last;\nMake a cofyne, close hit fast,\nFrye hit in oyle, sethe hit þou schalle\nAnd sugur and wyne ryȝt gode with alle.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Chewetes on flesshe daye.[/b]\nTake lyver of porke and kerve hit smalle,\nAs to a pye be hewen hit schalle,\nAnd hennes þerwith do alle in a panne,\nAnd frye hit wele as þou wele kanne;\nMake a cofyne as to smalle pye,\nDo þat þerin; and ȝolkes þerby\nOf harde egges sothun, and eke þou take\nPowder of gynger and salt to bake;\nKerve hit and frye hit in grece ful gode,\nWele pynchyd serve on last by þo rode,\nHere endes oure cure, þat I of spake,\nOf potage, hasteletes, and mete i bake\nAnd sawce þer to, with oute lesyng,\nCryst mot our sowles to hevene bryng.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Explicit hic quartus passus.[/b]\nOf petecure I wylle preche;\nWhat falles þer to ȝow wylle I teche;\nFore pore menne þys crafte is tolde\nÞat mowon not have spysory, as þay wolde;\nFor hit is nede to gode, to ken men gode\nAs wele þe pore as ryche by þo rode;\nÞerfore to telle you I am set,\nFyrst what herbȝ, with owtene let,\nBen gode to potage I wolle ȝow lere;\nÞou take þe crop of þo rede brere,\nRede nettel crop, and avans also,\nÞo prymrol, violet, þou take þerto\nTown cresses, and cresses þat growene in flode,\nClarray saveray and tyme gode wone,\nPersoley, wortes, oþer herbȝ mony wone;\nAlle þese erbs þou noȝt forsake,\nBut lest of prymrol þou shalle take.\nRede cole hane parte of potage is,\nFro Iuny to Sayn Iame tyde, iwys,\nÞenne leve his stade to Myȝellis eve,\nAnd þen bygynnys hit to releve;\nÞen þoroughe þe wyntur his curse schal holde,\nNeghe lentone seson þat porray be bolde.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For stondand fygnade.[/b]\nFyrst play þy water with hony and salt,\nGrynde blanchyd almondes I wot þou schalle;\nÞurghe a streynour þou shalt hom streyne,\nWith þe same water þat is so clene.\nIn sum of þe water stepe þou shalle\nWhyte brede crustes to alye hit with alle;\nÞenne take figgus and grynde hom wele,\nPut hom in pot so have þou cele;\nÞen take brede, with mylke hit streyne\nOf almondes þat be white and clene;\nCast in þo fyggus þat ar igrynde\nWith powder of peper þat is þo kynde,\nAnd powder of canel; in grete lordys house\nWith sugur or hony þou may hit dowce;\nÞen take almondes cloven in twen,\nÞat fryid ar with oyle, and set with wyn\nÞy disshe, and florysshe hit þou myȝt\nWith powder of gynger þat is so bryȝt,\nAnd serve hit forthe as I spake thenne\nAnd set hit in sale before gode menne.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For sirup.[/b]\nTake befe and sklice hit fayre and thynne,\nOf þo luddock with owte or ellis with in;\nTake mynsud onyouns, and powder also\nOf peper, and suet and befe þerto\nAnd cast þeron, rolle hit wele,\nEnbroche hit overtwert, so have þou cele;\nAnd rost hit browne as I þe kenne,\nAnd take brothe of fresshe flesshe þenne,\nand alye hit with bred er þou more do,\nAnd mynsud onyons þou cast þer to,\nWith powder of peper and clowes in fere;\nBoyle alle togeder, as I þe lere,\nÞenne boylyd blode take þou shalle;\nStrene hit þorowghe clothe, colour hit withalle;\nÞenne take þy rost, and sklyce hit clene\nIn þe lengethe of a fynger; boyle hit by dene\nIn þe same sewe; serve hit þou may
(English, XV c.)\n[b]In a disshe togedur I say.[/b]\nFor Tuskyn.\n\nTake raw porke and hew hit smalle,\nAnd grynde in a morter; temper hit þou schalle\nWith swongen egges, but not to þynne;\nIn gryndynge, put powder of peper withinne,\nÞenne þis flessh take up in þy honde,\nAnd rolle hit on balles, I undurstonde,\nIn gretnes of crabbes; I harde say\nIn boylande water þou kast hom may.\nTo harden þen take hom oute to cole,\nAnd play fresshe brothe fayre and wele;\nÞer in cast persoley, ysope, saveray,\nÞat smalle is hakked by any way.\nAlye hit with flour or brede for þy,\nColoure hit with safroun for þe maystré;\nCast powder of peper and clawes þer to,\nAnd take þy balles or þou more do,\nAnd put þer in; boyle alle in fere\nAnd serve hit forthe for tuskyne dere.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For blaunchyd porray.[/b]\nTake thykke mylke of almondes dere\nAnd heke hedes þou take with stalk in fere,\nÞat is in peses þou stryke;\nPut alle in pot, alye hit ilyke\nWith a lytel floure, and serve hit þenne\nWele soþun, in sale, before gode menne.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Porry of white pese.[/b]\nTake white pese and wasshe hom wele;\nPut hom in pot, so have þou cele,\nWith water; and ere þo fyrst boylyng\nÞou katche hom doune with oute lesyng;\nTrendel hom in platere and pyke hom clene,\nDevoyde þo worme -- etone alle bydene,\nIn fressh water þou schalt hom caste,\nAnd boyle hom wyle þat þey breste;\nSo sethe hom forthe al by dene,\nQuylle þay be boylde fayre and clene;\nÞen take þat brothe, and put þer to\nMynsyd onyons, with powder also\nOf peper, coloure hit with gode safroune,\nAnd put þer to a lytel porcioun\nOf ale, and sethe hit ryȝt wele, þenne\nAfter cut crust of bred I kenne,\nSware as dyse and put þerto;\nGyf hit a boylyng, no more ne myn,\nAnd serve hit forthe in to þe halle,\nÞese oþer peso ȝit make þou shalle.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For white pese after porray.[/b]\nTake boyled water wyth honey swete,\nSethe in þy pesone þat ben so sete,\nWhile þat þey lie be hom selfe þere\nWith mynsud onyons and no more,\nTo serve on fysshe day with grappays,\nWith sele fysshe or ellis with porpays,\nOpone fyssh dayes ȝif þat hit falle,\nÞus sethe þy pese I wot þou schalle;\nTemper hom in brothe of bacun clene\nAnd kepe þe gravé hit be not sene;\nȝif þay ben harde and wynnot alye\nBrysse hom or strene hom, Sir, wyturlye;\nThre leches of bacun lay þou mot\nIn brothe; and serve fulle wele þou wot\nWith þy pese, þat soþun ar wele,
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To ete þerwith, so have þou cele.[/b]\nFor Gray pese.\n\nFyrst stepe þy pese over þe nyȝt,\nAnd trendel hom clene, and fayre hom dyȝt.\nSethe hom in water; and brothe þou take\nOf bacun, and fresshe bre þou noȝt forsake;\nSumme men hom lofe alyed wyle\nWith floure and summe with never a dele;\nÞese pese with bacun eten may be\nAs þo whyȝt pese were, so mot I þe.\nBut þo white with powder of peper þo\nMoun be forsyd with ale þer to.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For kole.[/b]\nTake fresshe brothe of motene clene,\nOf vele and porke al by dene;\nHakke smalle þy wortis and persyl, þo\nWhen þat hit boylys, cast hom þerto,\nDo a lite grotes þy wortis amang\nAnd sethe hom forthe I undurstande.\nȝif þou have salt flesshe sethand I wot,\nTake a fresshe pece oute of þo pot,\nAnd sethe by þo self, as I þe kenne;\nTake up, put in þy wortis þenne,\nIn þe mene whyle gode gravé þou gete\nTo florisshe þy wortis at þo last hete.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For mustul bre.[/b]\nFyrst sethe þy mustuls quyl shel of lepe\nIn water, and þerof summe kepe;\nÞer in þou stepe white brede fayre,\nÞo remunaunde þou kepe with oute disware;\nAnd voyde þy groundyngus for sonde;\nPyke clene þy mustuls, wasshe hom with honde,\nSett hom besyde þy brede þou bray,\nTake mynsud onyons, and powdur I say\nOf peper, and cast þy bre into;\nColor hit with safroune er þou more do.\nAnd sethe hit wele; alye hit þenne\nWith þy forsayde brede, as I þe kenne,\nAl hole do in þy mustuls þore\nAnd serve hit forthe with outyn more.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For porray of mustuls.[/b]\nTake mustul brothe, as I say þe,\nAnd grynd þy lecus in morter fre,\nWith a lite grotes put hom þer in\nAnd sethe hom wele, no more no myn;\nBut grynde þy mustuls and put þer to\nAnd sethe alle up, now hase þou do.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For gruel of fors.[/b]\nFyrst take porke, wele þou hit sethe\nWith otene grotes, þat ben so smethe;\nWhenne hit begynnes wele to alye,\nþou save of þe þynnest brothe þer by\nTo streyne þy gruel, alle and summe;\nBut furst take oute þy porke þou mun\nAnd hak hit smal and grynde hit clene;\nCast hit to þo gruel þat streyned bene,\nColour hit with safroune and sethe hit wele;\nFor gruel of force serve hom at mele.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For Ioutes.[/b]\nTake most of cole, borage, persyl,\nOf plumtre leves, þou take þer tyl,\nRedde nettel crop and malues grene,\nRede brere croppes, and avans goode,\nA lytel nept violet by þo rode,\nAnd lest of prymrol levus þou take,\nSethe hom in water for goddes sake;\nÞenne take hom up, presse oute þou shalle\nÞe water, and hakke þese erbs alle\nAnd grynd hom in a morter schene\nWith grotene; and sethe hom thyk by dene\nIn fresshe brothe, as I þe kenne;\nTake sklyset, enbawdet þenne\nBesyde on platere þou shalt hit lay\nTo be cut and eten with ioutes in fay.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For capons in erbis.[/b]\nFyrst stop þy capone with saveray,\nWith persyl, a lytil ysope I say;\nÞen take þo neck, avoyde þe bone;\nAnd make a puddyng þer of anon\nWith an egge and myed bred also,\nWith hakked lyver and hert þer to,\nWith powder of peper and safroune; þen\nSew fast þo bylle grete ende, I ken;\nÞen sethe þy capone, as I þe say,\nWith persoley, sauge, ysope, saveray,\nA litel nep, brisse hom in hast\nAnd wrythe itwen; in hom þou cast\nWith sklices of bacon, enbrawdet here,\nAnd colour þy brothe with safrone dere.\nWhen hit is soþun, in disshe hit lay\nÞo bacon þo neck besyde in fay.\nTake grounden safron temperid with ale,\nTo florysshe þy capone with syder þou shalle,\nLyande in dysshe, and serve hym þenne,\nSet hym in sale before goode menne.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For oþer ioutes.[/b]\nTake cole and strype hom þorowghe þi honde\nAnd do away þo rybbys I undurstonde;\nIn fat bre fresshe of befe I wene,\nÞay schalle be soþun ful thykk by dene.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For honge cole.[/b]\nHakke þy kole wel grete I trow,\nSethe hom in water ful thyke I thrawe;\nÞen take hom up; presse a non\nÞe water of hom, er þou more done;\nIn dysshe hom hakke togeder þen\nWith buttur, to serve before gode men.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For henne in brothe.[/b]\nTake, sethe þy henne and kut her wele\nOn gobbettes, save alrons and þe pestle;\nSethe thritté egges harde also,\nAnd hakke þe white and cast þer to\nIn pot, with mynsud onyonus gode;\nFirst stepe þy brede of whete by þe rode,\nIn þe same brothe besyde to lye\nÞy sewe, in put powder of peper þer by\nOf clowes, of gynger þer to þou take,\nColoure hit with safroune for goddes sake;\nDo fyve ȝolkes in on disshe, þenne\nThre gobbettis of flesshe als of þat henne;\nPoure on þat sewe þat first was dyȝt,\nTo serve in sale by ful gode ryȝt.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For comyne sewe.[/b]\nȝiff þou wylle make a comyne sew,\nVele and motun and porke þou hew\nOn smalle gobettis; put hom in pot\nWith mynsud onyouns, ful wele I wot,\nAnd powder of Peper þou kast þerto;\nColoure hit with safroune or þou more do,\nAnd drawȝe alyoure of browne crust eke\nTo alye þis sew þat is so meke.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For a tansy cake.[/b]\nBreke egges in bassyn and swyng hem sone,\nDo powder of peper þer to anone;\nÞen grynde tansy, þo iuse owte wrynge,\nTo blynde with þo egges with owte lesynge.\nIn pan or skelet þou shalt hit frye,\nIn buttur wele skymmet wyturly,\nOr white grece þou make take þer to,\nGeder hit on a cake, þenne hase þou do,\nWith platere of tre, and frye hit browne.\nOn brode leches serve hit þou schalle,\nWith fraunche mele or oþer metis with alle.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For a froyse.[/b]\nSethe porke or vele and hew hit smalle,\nTake swongen egges and hew with alle;\nFrye hom in buttur in panne sone\nAnd styr hit wele, þen hase þou done.\nWith trowȝtes on þe same aray,\nWele soþun and hakked, tesyd in fay,\nAnd frye hom in buttur, as I þe kenne,\nTo serve on fysshe day before gode men.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For a brothe of elys.[/b]\nFyrst flyghe þyn elys, in pese hom smyte,\nPut hom in pot, þagh þay ben lyte,\nWith clene water; þen take þou schalle\nAlle powder of peper, coloure hit with alle\nWith safroune and alyed þenne\nWith floure, and cast alle in, I kenne,\nAt þe fyrst boylyng þat may falle
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Soth hote, and serve hit in to þe halle.[/b]\nFor a pye.\n\nFyrst sly þy capon over þo nyȝght,\nPlump hym in water wher he is dyȝt,\nAlle wallande hote anon take oute\nÞo capone to drye, with outen dowte;\nÞy stuffe of fressh befe mynse þou schalle\nWith wyne or verius or salt with alle,\nTo temper þat stuffe, and suet take þen\nOf þe same befe hakked I ken,\nThat suet þou coloure wiþ safroune wele\nIn a dysshe by hit selfe, as I þe telle;\nÞen lay þy capon in coffyn fyne,\nA mawdelarde þerby and wodcockys twyne,\nPut in þy stuffe er þou more done,\nWith an hen egge ȝolkes set hit anon,\nÞen take þy suet þat coloured was wele,\nMynge hit above, so have þou cele;\nÞen coloure þy capon with safroune, dore\nWith a feder, with a fayre feder, as I þe lore,\nSethyne, with clovyn dates ryȝt,\nWith maces and quibibis he shalle be dyȝt;\nCloves and graynys þou take þer to\nAnd raysyns of corauns forȝete not; þo\nClose on þy lyd and pynche hym þen,\nAnd bake hym forthe, as I þe ken.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For a cawdel.[/b]\nBreke ten egges in cup fulle fayre,\nDo away þe white with oute diswayre;\nÞo strene also þou put away\nAnd swyng þy ȝolkes with spone I þe say;\nÞen mynge hom wele with gode ale,\nA cup fulle large take þou schalle,\nSet hit on fyre, styr hit, I telle,\nBewar þer with þat hit never welle;\nȝif þou cast salt þer to, iwys\nÞou marres alle, so have I blis.\nAt þo fyrst assay þou take hit doun,\nWhen hit wolde welle, þys caudel broun,\nȝif þat hit welle, as may be falle,\nÞus helpe hit þen I wot þou schalle;\nStorve myed wastel with colde ale þen,\nAnd cast þer to, sethe hit I ken.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For sawce gynger.[/b]\nFyrst stepe þy brede, þat white is bake,\nAnd verius or venegur I undertake;\nÞen drawghe hit þorowghe a streynour fyne,\nColoure hit with safroune, and cast þer in\nPowder of gynger inoȝht, and salt,\nOr ellys coloure hit nouȝt þou schalt;\nFor grete lordis þou schalt take wyne\nWith safroune to þy sawce ful fyne.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For wesels.[/b]\nFyrst grynde porke, temper in fere\nWith egges and powder of peper dere,\nAnd powder of canel þou put þer to,\nIn chapon necke þou close hit þo,\nOr elles in paunche of grys hit pyt,\nAnd rost hit wele, and þen dore hit\nWith oute, with batere of egges and floure,\nTo serve in sale or ellys in boure.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For hagese.[/b]\nÞe hert of schepe, þe nere þou take,\nÞo bowel noȝt þou shalle forsake,\nOn þe turbilen made, and boyled wele,\nHacke alle togeder with gode persole,\nIsop, saveray, þou schalle take þen,\nAnd suet of schepe take in, I ken,\nWith powder of peper and egges gode wonne,\nAnd sethe hit wele and serve hit þenne,\nLoke hit be saltyd for gode menne.\nIn wyntur tyme when erbs ben gode,\nTake powder of hom I wot in dede,\nAs saveray, mynt and tyme, fulle gode,\nIsop and sauge I wot by þe rode.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For seke menne.[/b]\nAle bre þus make þou schalle,\nWith grotes and safroune and good ale.\nTake playd water with hony, I wote,\nFor water gruel made with grote;\nMelle white brede in dysshes aboute,\nPowre in wellyd mylke, with outen doute,\nÞat called is mylke soppys in serves\nFor Satyrday at nyȝt, so have I blys.\nȝet sugurt soppes I nyl forȝete,\nÞou tost shyves of gode manchete,\nEnbene hom with wyne on both syde; þenne\nSawce hom with sugur inoȝhe I kenne.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For sethe ray.[/b]\nTake ote, strey and draghe hit clene,\nCouch hit in a panne with water by dene;\nCast salt þer to, ley in þy ray,\nAnd set hit forthe as I þe say:\nThen take hit oute, þo skyn away,\nSouse hit in ale, and salt, I pray;\nWhen hit is colde, ete hit þou may\nWith lyver and garlek, þat samen are dyȝght.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Oystere in browet.[/b]\nTake and schole hom and sethe hom in clene water;\nGrynde peper and safroun with brede and ale, temper hit\nUp with þe same brothe, and do þe oysters þer in, and\nLet hit boyle and cast salt þerin and messe hit forthe.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For a servise on fysshe day.[/b]\nFyrst white pese and porray þou take,\nCover þy white heryng for goddys sake;\nÞen cover red heryng and set abufe,\nAnd mustard on heghe, for goddys lufe;\nÞen cover salt salmon on hast,\nSalt ele þer wyth on þis course last.\nFor þe secunde course, so god me glad,\nTake ryse and fletande fignade,\nÞan salt fysshe and stok fysshe take þou schalle,\nFor last of þis course, so fayre me falle.\nFor þe iii cours sowpys dorre fyne,\nAnd also lampronus in galentyne,\nBakun turbut and sawmon ibake\nAlle fresshe, and smalle fysshe þou take\nÞer with, als trouȝte, sperlynges and menwus with al,\nAnd loches to hom sawce versance shal.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For a servise on flesshe day.[/b]\nFyrst wortes and salt befe þou shalle have,\nWith capon in erbe þer to I crawe;\nFor þo fyrst cours, no more þou take,\nBut of þe secunde course now wylle I clake.\nFyrst take in selle, þan gose anon,\nBothe grys and vele and rostyd motone;\nWith gynger þo pigge eton shalle be,\nAnd sorel with þo moton so mot I þe.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For anoþer maner of service on flesshe day.[/b]\nTake fyrst grete pyes and frumenté\nWith venison, so mot I þe,\nAnd rostyd capon, þen shal þou take,\nÞys for þe fyrst cours, þou noȝght forsake;\nThen fylets in galentine and mortrews eke\nWith rostyd befe and moton so meke,\nAnd rosted vele and porke and grys;\nAnd gose and gryce for secunde be wyse,\nFor the thrydde cours, now take shalle\nCawdel ferre, stued mawdelarde with alle,\nThen tarts and daryels and custan dere,\nRysshene and pome dorres, and frutur in fere,\nThenne rosted mawlarde and cele þer to,\nWith wodcoke and oþer smalle bryddys inow.\nOf servis tel ȝou no more I wylle,\nFor a comyne fest at home be skylle.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For a comyn rewle in cure.[/b]\nNow tas þys for a rewle fulle gode,\nAll hole futed fuylle in flud\nGose before, and ay þou take\nÞo grettis fyrst, savun gose and drake,\nBothe of towne and of toþer,\nAlso bakyn mete, my der brother,\nAnd most daynté, come byhynde:\nÞys is a rewle mad in kynde.
(English, XIV c.)\nAlmond milk, rice flour, capon meat, sifted ginger, white sugar, white wine; each one in part to be boiled in a clean pot, and then put in the vessel in which it will be done, a little light powder; pomegranates planted thereon.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Vert desirree.[/b]\nAlmond milk, rice flour, capon meat, red wine, sugar, parsley; the color will be green.
(English, XIV c.)\nAlmond milk, rice flour, capon meat; blanched almonds fried and put therein, blanched almonds planted thereon; the color will be yellow with saffron.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Viaunde d'Espyne.[/b]\nAlmond milk, rice flour, capon meat, ground pistachios in part planted thereon; powder of cloves put therein, so give it a good flavor of the ground pistachios; color, yellow.
(English, XIV c.)\nWine, amidon, seedless raisins put therein, sugar to cut down the strength of the wine.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Haucegeme.[/b]\nAlmond milk, rice flour, ground veal, veal diced and put therein, galingale, cinnamon, sugar: color, red of dragon's blood.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Maumenee.[/b]\nWine, capon meat ground all to powder and then put therein to boil in the wine; ground almonds all dried and put therein; powder of cloves put to all, little bits of almonds must be put therein, it must be coarsely ground meat, sugar to cut the strength of the spices; color, red or light blue.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Double mortrels.[/b]\nAlmond milk, eggs, a little amidon, galingale, ginger; hard boiled eggs divided into small pieces and put therein, sugar, crushed wafers planted thereon: color, yellow.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Poumes ammolee.[/b]\nWine, eggs, wheat flour, apples fortified thereon, sugar to cut the strenght of the wine.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Coudree en temps de nois.[/b]\nAlmond milk, rice flour, fried kernels, sifted ginger, sugar to cut the bitterness, nuts planted thereon.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Spynete.[/b]\nAlmond milk, hawthorn flowers softened in almond milk, and that will have good flavor of the flowers; and amidon, coarse meat, sifted ginger, sugar to cut the strength of the ginger, white flowers planted thereon.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Rosee.[/b]\nAlmond milk, rose petals that it will taste all of roses, cinnamon, rice flour or amidon; coarse meat; powder of cinnamon, sugar; the color of roses; rose petals planted thereon.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Fryseye.[/b]\nStrawberries softened in almond milk, rice flour or amidon, coarse meat, powder of cinnamon, and sugar; color red; strawberries planted thereon.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Sirisee.[/b]\nAlmond milk thickened with amidon, ground cherries without the stones, some sugar here that it has a good flavor of cherries; coarse meat; cherries planted thereon; color, red.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Browet d'Alemaigne.[/b]\nTake almond milk, sifted cloves of gillyflowers, cubebs, fried onions; and it must be hot with cloves and cubebs; color, yellow.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Browet sek.[/b]\nSweet broth, grape verjuice, ground parsley put therein, cloves, mace, cubebs; in times of chicks after Easter; and it will have the taste of good spices, saffron cooked therein with parsley in the broth; color, yellow.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Browet Sarasyneys blanc.[/b]\nCow's milk thickened with eggs, planted with large sifted ginger; in the season of new apples; color, white.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Browet salmenee.[/b]\nVinegar, galingale, cinnamon, powder of cloves of gillyflowers in great abundance; soft eggs, and sugar in great abundance to cut the strength of the spice; thick with the spice of ginger; color, black or green.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Soree.[/b]\nWine, water, fresh eels, and other manner of fish; fried eels, the liver withheld, the gobbets powdered in cinnamon; color, red.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Dragonee.[/b]\nAlmond milk, rice flour, capon meat, sugar, cinnamon; color, red of dragon's blood.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Pynetee.[/b]\nWine, sugar, boiled together; ginger and honey; powder of ginger and cloves; garnish abundantly with pine nuts; and dress it in coffins of chestnut flour; color, yellow of saffron.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Diacre.[/b]\nAlmond milk, amidon, sifted rice flour, capon meat, a great abundance of powder of ginger, sugar, white wine, alkanet, fresh wafers planted thereon; color, red.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Swade.[/b]\nAlmond milk, amidon or the thickened with elderflowers; The flowers must be plucked and put in a great abundance of ginger; elderflowers planted thereon; color, white.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Raunpant perree.[/b]\nPears cooked in water thicked with eggs or amidon; planted thereon with leaves of dried dough, color yellow, with three rampant lions on the scales.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Gelee.[/b]\nFish cooked in wine an in water, and saffron, powdered ginger, cinnamon, galingale; and put in a clean, covered vessel; color, white.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Brasee.[/b]\nSpiced wine, cinnamon, the fish sprinkled and planted in a frying pan or a peel with cubebs and cloves, and roasted on a griddle, then boil in wine and spices; color, red.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Teste de Tourk.[/b]\nSheet of dough, good wheat: plant therein, coneys and birds, pitted dates soaked in honey, new cheese planted therein, cloves, cubebs, sugar therein, then a layer of pistachio stuffing abundantly; color of stuffing, red, yellow and green. The head should be dressed black in the manner of the hair of women in a black braid, a face of a man thereon.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Viaunde de Cypre.[/b]\nAlmond milk, rice flour, powder of ginger that it will smell strongly of ginger; and that it will be planted with ginger ground pistachios; color, yellow.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Ermynee.[/b]\nWill be made white and well flavored of good powder of ginger, and of cubebs and of cloves, and the meat must be part vert desirree.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Sang dragoun.[/b]\nAlmond milk and of rice, and good powder of ginger and sugar; color of dragon's blood.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Hauseleamye.[/b]\nVine grapes, hock of sheep; when these two things have been boiled together, in a little broth or verjuice, so much must be well strained and clean; then take the March chicken and chop it, and put it in to boil; and when it is well boiled, put a great amount of powdered ginger to remove the bitterness of the grapes. Color is green.
(English, XIV c.)\n[b]Moree.[/b]\nrice flour or amidon, whichever can be found; that the color of sandalwood will be had, grind well in a mortar; and then it must be tempered in almond milk and well strained. And then put powdered cinnamon and of galingale. If it is a fish day, put in pears or chestnuts or salmon, or luce or perch; if a meat day, put in veal or goat, if you would have a good and royal meat.
(English, XV c.)\n[b](untitled)[/b]\nTake caules and stryp hem fro the stalkes and betes borage an ane vyolet malves percely betayn prymrose paciens the wyghthe lekes croppes of netels perboyle hem & ley hem on a borde presse out the watyr hewe hem small and do ther to otemele take the broth of the congure turbut othir good fysche as of salmon do hit in a pott withe the foresaid herbes when the broth ys at the boylyng caste in the wortys & the herbes boyle hem up loke they be salte and yf thou lacke brothe boyle elys take hem up stripp of the fysch from the bonys grynd hit tempre hit with the selfe broth do al to gedyr in a pott un to the wortys be forsayd & boyle hem up also then mayste yf thou wil sethe mustulis sett hem over the fyre and do to hem as moche watyr as thay may flete yn boyle hem tyll they opyn then poure oute the broth thorow a streynour pyke the mustulys grynd hem tempere hem up with the silfe broth and draw hem thorough a streynour take the same manner of herbes as thu dedist by fore and the broth of the mustulys sette on the fyre boyle hem up when the herbes be boyled y nought caste in the mustulys drowe yn salte and yf thou wylte thou mayste draw pesyn thorow a streynere and make up the wortys with fayre watyr put ther yn clere oylle lete them be frydd in by fore the boylyng & lay up with the forsayde peson and lete none ottemele come ther yn also thou mayste yf thow will perboyle the white of lekeys and presse out the watyr hew them smalle take canbenys and fayre watyr & sett hem on the fyre & when they boyle doyn the white of lekys loke none ottemele come ther yn salt them & serve them forth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]For to make canabenes[/b]\nTake white benes ley hem in watyr rennyng too days and change the watyr take hem & ley hem dry then dry hem hard uppon a ston or a pon a este than shylle them atte a tjylle and do a way the evehys and close the benys iij or iiij at the most and then make hem clene and so may thou kepe hem as longe as thou wylte.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Canabens[/b]\nTake kanbens wesch hem and yf thu wilte stoppe hem a lytyll & make hem up with mylke of almondys put ther to sugure and salt out of lentyn make hem up with cowe mylke and put ther to sygure and salte and buttyrr claryfyde.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Canabens With Bacon[/b]\nDo suete brothe yn a potte wesche the canabens clene and do ther to and boyle yt up put no lykure ther to loke thay be salte & serve hem take ribbys of bacon boylyd do a way the skyn and ley hem on a dysch and serve hem forther as ye serve venson yn brothe.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Butturd Wortys[/b]\nTake al maner of good herbes that thu mayste gete peke hem wesche hem hewe hem boyle hem in fayre watyr put buttyr ther to claryfyyd a grete dell when they be boylyd y now salte hem lete non otemele come ther yn dyse brede too smale gobettys and do yn dyschys and powre there wortys ther upon and serve hem forth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Cabogys[/b]\nTake white cabogys kutt hem fro the stalkes in grete pesys weche hem clene perboyle hem wesch presse out the watyr and hew hem but a lytyll and in flesch tyme do fayre broth of beth or of caponys or of othir good flesch in a potte when hit boylleth do ther to thi cabochis and mary bonys al to brokyn boile hit up do ther to safron and salt when hit ys boyllyd y now alay hit up with gratyd bredde and boylle yt a lytyll and serve hit forth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Hare or goose powdryd in wortys[/b]\nTake good brothe of beef and of othir good flesh & mary bonys do hit in a potte sett hit ovyr the fuyre chop an hare in pecys and do ther to and yf thu wille weshe hym yn the same broth that thu wille boyll hym yn then draw the broth thorow a strayner with all the blod then take caulys & the white of lekys and othyr herbes and ottemele and hew hem small to gedyr and yf hit be an olde hare lete hym boyle well or thu caste yn the wortys yf he be a yonge hare cast hym and thy wortys to gadyr also take a goose of a day and a nyght powdryng chop here & put here in the wortys yn the same maner.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Joutys yn flesch days[/b]\nTake kawlys & percelly and othir good herbes perboyle hem welle yn watyr presse out the watyr hew hem ryght smalle or grynd hem and yf thu wylte thu may hew a lytylle fat porke ther wyth and grynd hit ther with and temper hit up with swete porke loke hit be sum delle chaungant of the herbes do yt in a pot boyle & halye hit up a lytyll ther with and yf thu wylte thou may draw bredde with sum of the brothe then salt hem and serve hem forth with ribbys of bacon or with fat flesch yf thu wylte and one fysch days thu may perboyle herbes & make hem up in the same maner with broth of fresch fysch or elys with thykke mylke of almondys and sigure & salt and lete non othir lykure come there yn.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Lentyn foyles[/b]\nTake the same maner of herbes as thu dost to jowtys and onyons clere paryd perboyle hem presse out the watyr do hem yn a potte frye reysons in clere oyle that have be fryed yn byfore and do ther to with a perty of the oyle and boyle hit up with the mylke of almondys and put ther to sugure & salte.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Longe wortys[/b]\nTake the same maner of herbes boyle peson take hem fro the fyre take out the cleryst and make hem with the same maner of thyngys save sygure and serve hit.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Blaunche pore[/b]\nTake thyke melke of almondys do yt in a potte perboyle the whyte of lekys tendour presse out the watyre hew hem smalle grynd hem temper hem with the same mylke do to gedyr with sygure and salt boyle hit up yf thu wilte thu mayste alay with payndemayn othir with cromys of white brede draw hem with the same mylke and serve hit forth with salte ele yf thu have hit.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Pome perre[/b]\nBoyle white pesyn hool hem take hem fro the fyre when they have restyd a whyle then take the cleryst in to a nothir pott then have mylke of almond drawyn up with wyen figes of amely sigure and salte and yf thou wylte reysons fryed w lytyll & do to gedyr boyle hit kepe hit and serve hit forth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Gingaudre[/b]\nTake the hedde of hake fysch the sound and the lever do hit in a pott to gadyr make clene the poke of the sayd hake and do hit ther to sethe hit well in brothe of the selfe fisch or fayre watyr tyll hit be tendour then take yt up lay hit on a bord peke a wey the bondys & safe the fysch hole dyse the lever & the sound yf the poke be not tendour y now sethe hit bettyr and do hit to gedyr kut white brede temper hit with the same brothe and wyne draw hit thorow a lyour put yn a pott put ther to poudyr of pepyr gynger and poudyr of canell and a good colour of sandryn set hit on the fyre ster hit when hit boyleth put hit in the fysch and ster hit esely for brekyng and sesyn hit up with powdyr of gynger and a lytyll venyger & salt then lete hytt no more boyle thu may yf thu wilte take the sound and the lever & the poke of the codlyng and make hit in the same manere.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Eles yne sorre[/b]\nFle eles chop hem yn gobenys do hem yn a potte with onyons and herbes hew hem to gedyr with hole clowys macys powdyr of pepyr powdyr of canell a grete dele & fayre watyr & draw lyour of bredde with wyn do hit to gedyr sett hit on the fyre ster hit when hit ys boyled y now colowr hit up with sawndrys sesyn hit withe poudyr of gynger venyger & salt and lete hit no more boyle.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Pykes or elys in ballocbroth[/b]\nSplett pykes scale hem clene & culpon eles small put hem yn a potte put ther to onyons mynsyd grete & herbes sese hem up with a lyour of bredd and put to hem stockefysch put ther to macys & clowys and powdyr of canell y nowe and a lytyll saveryn and put to hem stockfysch a qutte lyk un to and lete the pyke seth in a esy sause & serve hole pykys for lordys & quarters for othir men & culpons loke they be sesynde yn kynde and put broth y now upon the pyke & serve hym forth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Frumente yn lentyn[/b]\nTake clene pykyd whete bray hit yne a morter and fanned clene & seth hit tyl hit be brokyn than grynd blaunch almondys yn a morter draw ther of a mylke do hit to gedyr & boyle hit tyl hit be resonabulle thykke than loke thy whete be tendyr colour hit up with safferyn leche thy purpas when hit ys sodyn than ley hitt on dysches by hit sylfe and serue hit forth withe frumente.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Pylets yn sarcene[/b]\nTake fresch porke or motyn sodyn peke out the bonys hew the flesch small & grynd hit smal yn a morter and temper hit with eyron yn the gryndyng putt ther to pepyr safferyn & salt take fresch broth clene tryed set yt over the fyre in large vessell lete hit boyle then sesyn hit with the same colour then make smal rounde ballys put hem yn a boylyn broth & lete hem boyle ther yn tyll they be y now then take hem up lete hem drye lete thy broth keyl blow of the fat take almondys wesch hem temper hem up with the same broth draw ther of a kynd mylke put the mylke in a swete potte set hit on the fyre put ther to powdyr of pepyr & canell & a pertyon of sawndrys to colour hit sarcene colour loke thy most colour be of hys owne kynde put ther yn clowys macys reysons of coraunce lete hit boyle as thy seyyst that good ys yf hit be tt thike a lay hit with swete wyne and do ther to sugur when thy spycez beth tendour put yn peletys in the same broth ghyf hym atarage of poudyr of pepyr of gynger and vergys & serve forth the pelets with the bruet iij or iiij yn a dysche as a potage for the secunde course.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To make Jussall[/b]\nTake swete broth of capons or elys or broth as thu may have set hit on the fyre in a brode vessell colour hit with saveryn put sage ther to out grote and saffron breke eyron styr hem well to the eyron and to thy herbes be mellyd to gedyr when hit be gynnys to seth take out thy potstyke and turne ty crud aboute with the scome loke thy fyre be not to hasty wh whene hit ys thorow knyt take hit of the fyr and cover hit & serve hit forth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To make leche lardys of iij colours[/b]\nTake clene cow mylke and put hit in iij pottys breke to everych a queantyte of eyron as thu seist best ys to do rede colour with saundres & a nothyr with saveryn the iij with grene herbys put to everych a porcyon of clene larde of fat of bacon well sodyn & pertyd in iij pottys put to salt boyle hem all at ones stere hem well for brennyng yn the boylyng take hem downe cast hem in to a cloth everych a bove other and wynd the cloth to gedyr & presse out all the juse than take hem out all hole and make leches of hem and do iij or iiij leches in a dysch and serve hem forth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]To make umbelys of a dere[/b]\nTake the umbelys of a dere blod & all perboyle hem in fresch broth then take hem up stale broune crustys of brede in the same broth then cut thy umbelys small & put hem in a potte to the same broth tryyd in a streynour sesyn hym ther with that they be kyndky rennyng do to pepyr canell & tempyr hit up with swete wyne put hit to the umbelys loke thy colour stond by the canell sesyn hit with salt & serve hit forth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Grewel enforsed[/b]\nTake merybonys & fresch beef make good gruell ther of than draw hem thorow a streyner take fayre porke tender sodyn peke out the bonys & the senowys & do a wey the skyn grynd hit smal yn a morter temper hit up with the same gruell that ys grownd make hit smothe let hit stond resonabely by the flesshe sesyn hit up with salt & saferyn that sette hym by the fyre lete hym boyle a lytyll and serve hym forthe.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Chaudon of Salmon[/b]\nTake al the draught of a samon make hit clene as thu may do hit yn a pote and al the blod of a samon ther with boyle that tyl hit be y nowghe yn the broth of the same fysch take hit up hew hit smalle yf hit be a femaule grynde the spaun do hit to gedyr to the broth draw a lyour of white bredde with swete wyne do ther to poudyr of peper & canell sett hit on the fyre stere hit when hit boylez seson hit up with powdyr of gyngyr venyger salt & safferyn thu may serve hit forth yn the stede of potage or els sause of samon.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Cokkes of kellyng[/b]\nTake cokkes of kellyng cut hem smalle do hit yn a brothe of fresch fysch or of fresch salmon boyle hem well put to mylke and draw a lyour of bredde to hem with saundres safferyn & sygure and poudyr of pepyr serve hit forth & othyr fysch amonge turbutt pyke samon choppyd & hewyne sesyn hem with venyger & salt.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Felets yn galentyne[/b]\nTake the ribbys of a breste of porke fle of the skyn do the flesche on a broche roste hit tyl hit be almost ynowghe take hit of chop hit yn pecys do hit yn a potte with onyons cut grete wyth clowys hole macyz quibibys do to gedyr & a quantyte of swete broth draw a lyour of paryngys of crystys of white bredde with good wyne and a lytyll blod & alaye hit a lytyll & do ther to poudyr of pepyr a lytyll & a good quantyte of poudyr of canell loke that hit be nott chargaunt sesyn hit up with poudyr of gynger & salt venyger & salt.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Leche proven[/b]\nTake mylke of almondyes tempyr hit wyth wyn white wyne and take watyr percellye & oynons cut do ther to elys choppyd & boyled do ther yn saferon & hole pepyr & hole clowys seson hit up with powdyr & salt.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Numbelys of purpas or of other fysche[/b]\nPerboyle the numbelys of purpays & thu wylte sum of the fysch cut hit smalle do hit yn a pott draw a lyour of crustys with brede wyth the same broth & som what of the blod and red wyn do hit to geder yn a potte with powder of gynger clowys and canell boyll hit stere hit seson hit up with powder of gynger venygger and salt. Make numbelys of codlyng in the same maner and of other gode fyssh also & serve them forthe.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Purpays yn Galanteyn[/b]\nTake purpays do a way the skyn cutt hit yn smal lechys no more then fynger or els take bred drawen wyth red wyne put there to powder of canell powdyr of pepyr boil al seson hit up wyth powder of gynger venegre & salt.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Purpays or Venyson in broth[/b]\nTake chikenys of purpas and more of the fysch yf thu wylte chopp hit in pecys with onyons & herbes cut grete & hole clowys & macys powdyr of pepyr & canell & do to gedyr in a pott wythe fayre watyr or with broth of the fysch and with a perty of wyne boyle hit up yf the fysch be goode hit wille a lay hit sylfe or els draw a lytyll lyour of crustys & do ther to poudyr of gynger & salt and make venyson in broth in the same maner.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Hare yn cyve[/b]\nSmyte a hare in small pecys perboyle hem yn swete broth with hys own blodd cast hym yn a cold watyr peke hym clene do hym yn a pott claryfyd claryfye the broth clene do ther to onyons & herbes mynsyd take hole clowys macys & powdyr & draw ther yn a lyour of crustys with rede wyne boyle hit tyl hit be ynowghe sesyn hit up with powdyr of gynger venyger & salt & loke hit be a good colour of blod.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Hare yn papald[/b]\nTake a hare chop hym pecys perboyle hym yn watyr claryfe the broth put to thy flesch boyle hyt seson hit up with douce poudyr & salt take losyngez of past frydd of wafrons cowch hem in a dysches & poudyr the sewe a boyvyn.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Hare yn talbut[/b]\nChoppe a hare yn pecys perboyle hym yn good broth with hys owne blode trye the flesch yn a potte grynd almondys unblaunched tempyre hem up with the same brothe & put mylke there to and do therto onyonys perboyld hole spicer and powdyr for the sesyn hit up poudir and salt a quantite of wyne and a lytil sugur.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Conynggez in grave[/b]\nPerboile conyngges in gode brothe take them up smyte them in peces make hem clene do hem in a pott with hole clowis macys & onyons y cut somedel grete in pouder blaunche almondys grynd hem & draw up withe the same brothe a thike mylke & do to gedyr suger boyle hit loke hit be salt messe hit forthe cast ther on a dragge of clowys macys a mynsyd gynger and blaunch poudyr.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Conynggez in Cyve[/b]\nChop conyngys in pecys do hem in a pott take onyons and good herbes y choppyd to gedyr boyle hem up in swete brothe do ther to poudyr of pepyr make a lyour of paryngys of crustys of swete bredde drawyn with wyn and a lytle blode alay hit up but a lytyll do ther to poudyr of canele a grete dele sesyn hit up with poudyr of gynger wenggur & salt.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Conyngges yne clere broth[/b]\nChop conyngys in pecys wesche hem clene do hem yn a pott put ther to clene broth & rede wyne boyle hem till they be y nowghe loke hit nowght much of the broth sesyn hit up with poudyr of gynger a grete quantyte and vergyes and draw hit thorow a streynoure loke hit be salt & serve hit forthe.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Oysters in grave[/b]\nSchelle oystrys in to a pott and swette ther with put ther to fayre watyr perboyle hem take hem up put hem yn fayre watyr peke hem clene blaunch almondys grynd hem tempyr heme up with the same broth draw up a good mylke do hit in a pott with onyons and hole spycez and a lytyll poudyr of sygure boyle hit to gedyr & doo the oystres ther to & serve hit forth & caste ther yne youre dragge of hole spicys a bovyn & blaunche poudyr.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Oystres yn Cyve[/b]\nShele oystrys perboyle hem in fayre watyr and the selfe owet & wasch hem yn fayre watyr pyke and trye the broth thorow a streynoure do to gedyr make hem up as thy dyd the conyngys al save the blod & colour hem with saunders.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Chikens in gretney[/b]\nBoyle chikens in broth good broth and rese the thyys and the wyngys & the brestys take mylke of almondys unblanched draw up withe the same brothe & poudyr of canell & a perty of wyne sygure saffron & salt do hit to gedyr yn a pott set on the fyre stere hit when hit boyles sesyn hit up with poudyr of gynger & vergeus lay the chikenys hote yn dysches have yolkes of eyron sodyn hard & fryed a lytyll couche on a boute the wyngez & the thyes.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Creteyney[/b]\nTake capons and othir fowlys perboile hem dyse hem cast hem yn a pott with cowe mylke &amp; boyle hit ther withe drawe payndmayne withe som of the mylke and put to gedyr take sodyn eyron hew the white & cast ther to sesyn hit up with poudyr sigure & safferyn & salt and a ley hit up with yolkes of eyron sodyn hard & frye hem a lytyll ley hem in disches poure the sewe a bovyn and floresch hit withe anneys in comfite.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Capons yne conceps[/b]\nTake capons halfe rostyde do hem yn a pott put ther to swete broth & a perty of rede wyne stew hit up to gedyr that hit be ynowghe trye the brothe yf thu wylte thu may do ther to a lytyll lyoure of payndemayn take eyron sodyn harde hew the white do ther to sigure safron & salt set hit on the fyre when hit boyles a lay hit up withe yolkes of eyron loke hit be rennyng sesyn hit up withe poudyr of gynger & vergeys a rese the thyys & the whyngez & the brestz of the capons loke that they honge by ley hem yn disches plante hem withe hard yolkes of eyron and poudyr & the sewe a bovyn.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Chikens yne caudell[/b]\nTake chikens & perboyle hem yn good licoure tyl they be ynowghe coloure the brothe with safron take up the chikens rese the whyngez and the thyys & the brestys a ley up the broth with yolkez of eyron in the maner of a caudell sesyn hit up with sygure & salt couche the chikens yn dishches & dresse the sewe a bovyn & strew on poudyr of gynger & serve hit forthe.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Soupes[/b]\nTake marye do hit yn a pot with hony poudyr of pepyr poudyr of gynger canell & a leye hit take brede cut hit yn gobettys tost hem couche hem yn dysches loke thy syryp be salt ghyf hit a colour of safron and serve hit forthe.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Chaudon of Veel[/b]\nTake the bowels of veel make hem clene seth them in fresshe brothe cut hem smalle take pouder and wyne or veneger and alay hit with brede take past of flour of whete and make pelettez and them in grece and put to geder.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Chaudon of Pigges fete[/b]\nTake swynes fete clene scallyd the groyne and the erys boylid in fresshe brothe take hem up kut them smalle do hit in a potte trye the brothe drawe a thyn lyoure of white brede and wyne and put hit to gedire and make a thyn foyle of past cutt yn smale pelettez frye them seson them up wyth pouder of pepire and safron and salt and do the pelettez hote in dysshes and do the sewe a bove.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Bonse desire[/b]\nTake blaunche almondez grynde them drawe them up wyth swete brothe and swete wyne do ther do a quantite of white sugur do hit in a pott and cast ther do take porke wel sodyn tender and grynde hit smalle and medill hit wyth yolkys of eyron pouder and salt and make pelettes ther of the gretnys of the yolke have a bature of yolkes of eyron & paryd floure turne the pelets ther yn take hem frye hem rolle hem up in a panne that they may be round lay ham hote yn dysches dresse the sewe a bovyn loke hit be renyng and on do the fisch dayes thou may withe pike haddok or codlyng do in the same maner.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Bruet of lumbardy[/b]\nTake hennys chikens conyngys or othere flesch sodyn do hit in a morter do ther to mylke of almondys do ther in pepyr and alay hit with bredde & do ther in yolkes of eyron sodyn hard growndyn & drawyn up withe percelly & do ther to a lytyll grece or claryfyd boture or the fat of porke & sesyn hit up with poudyr salt & venyger & make hit rede as blod.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Bruet of Almayn[/b]\nTake beef or porke chopyd in pecys cast hem yn a pott grynd almondys draw hem with swete brothe & put hit yn the flesch boyle hit & put ther to poudyr of pepyr & sygure when hit ys yboyled y nowghe sesyn hit up with poudyr of gynger & vergeys & coloure hit al rede as blode with.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Bruet of Spayne[/b]\nCut venson yn longe leches & frye hem or rost hem with poudyres weshe hem in wyne take sygure & mylke of almondys clowys macyz and quibibis boyle hit to gedyr & seson hit up with poudyr & venyger.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Bruet roos[/b]\nTake the flesch of a roo chop hit perboile hit trye hit and do hit yn a potte take the same broth or othir swete broth draw thorow a streynour & put hit to flesch with onyons ande herbis & hole clowys macys & quibibis & boyle hit & yf be nede alay hit with crustys or els with white brede & with a lytyll of the same broth & of the same blod colourd with safron salt & with poudyr of pepyr & more of canelle & serve hit forth make al othir sewys in the same maner.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Chikens yn bruet[/b]\nTake chikens colord & trye the broth in til a pot wyn & sygure do ther to & seson hit up with poudyr of gynger vergeys & canelle that ys drawyn thorowz a streynour & colour hit with saffron.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Stewe lumbard[/b]\nTake porke rost hit chop hit and do hit yn a pott & wyn & sygur & hole onyons clowys gynger saffron & saunders & almondys fryyd & temperyz hit up withe poudyr of gynger galentyn & canell coloure hit with saffron & saunders the chese and other stewyd lumbardys grynd almondys draw hem up with swete broth take veele & porke & pare hit clene from the skyn hew hit smalle grynd hit & medyl hit with mynsyd datys reysons of corans and and gode powder stere hitt welle when hit boyleth make hitt in pelettz as grete as a plome sette the mylke on the fyre styre hitt wel when hitt boylyth cast in the pelettez and lette hit stewe up on the fyre and do the to powdir and salt and serve hyt forthe.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Stewy colops[/b]\nTake colops of venyson rostyd do hem yn a pott do wyn ther to hole spycez & poudyr of pepyr & canell boyle hit up weth a perty of swete brothe sesyn hit up with poudyr of gynger & venyger & serve hit forth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Bruet tuskyn[/b]\nTake broth of capons & of marybonys & of othir goode flesch do hit yn a pott chop chikenys yn pecys and herbes & hole clowys macys poudyr of pepur do hit to gedyr set hit on the fyre grynd porke & wele rawe with yolkes of eyron sodden hard put ther ro reysons of coraunse poudour& salt & saffron & medyl hit to gedyr & set hit on the fyre & when youre pott boylez make hit in pelets as grete as notys cast hem yn the boylyng & coloure hit with juyse of percelley & of othir good herbes boyle hit up & put ther to a lytyll good wyne sesyn hit up with poudyr of gynger & venyger & serve hit forth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Bruet sarcenes[/b]\nTake venyson boyle hit trye hit do hit yn a pott take almond mylke drawyn up with the same brothe cast ther yn onyons & a ley hit up withe floure of rye & caste yn cloves aftyr the boylyng take hit don sensyn hit up with poudyr wyn & sygure & coloure hit with alekenet.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Bruet of kedes[/b]\nTake a kede welle chopyd perboyled & tryed do hit yn a pott take almondys & do ther to that ys draw up wyth fresche broth do ther to hole cloves & aley hit up with floure of rye & do ther yn grece and aftyr the boylyng sesyn hit up with venyger poudyr of pepyr gynger & canel & sygure & salt & cast ther to.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Blaunch Bruet[/b]\nTake hennys or porke rostd & chopyd do hit yn a pott do almonde mylke ther to aley hit up with floure of rye do ther yn a lytyll broth & a quantyte of wyne clovys & macys & sesyn hit up with venyger & pouderes & a lytyll sygure strenyned with alekenet.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Sauce sarcenes[/b]\nMake a thykke mylke of almondys do hit in a pot with floure of rye safrone gynger macys quibibis canel sygure & rynse the bottom of the disch with fat broth boyle the sewe byfore & messe hit forth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Veel in bucnade[/b]\nChop vele in pecys do hit in a pot do ther to onyons cut grete & herbes & good pouderez clovys macyz sygure safron & salt & boyle hit with a lytyll swete broth than put ther to good cow mylke boyle hit up with yolkes of eyron lete hit be rennyng & serve hit forth & make hit with cowe mylke in this maner a fore sayd & thu mayste make hit with almond mylke in the same maner and when hit ys boyled sesyn hit up withe poudyr of gynger & vergeys.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Pynonad[/b]\nTake mylke of almond drawyn with swete broth do ther to pynes a grete dele then take wardons quinsys & costardys sodyn & groundyn and drawyn thorow a streynour withe wyne & good pouders do to gedyr boyle hit serve hit forth.
(English, XV c.)\n[b]Kyd stewyd[/b]\nTake a kydde & yf thu will thu may roste hit a lytill or also chop hit raw in pecys do ther to onyons & herbes & swete broth & wyne hole clovys macys & othir pouderys & stew hit to gedyr sesyn hit up with the same gynger or galentyn & with a lytyll lyour of bred safron & salt & serve hit forth.
